column6: Nokia X2 review after 2 months of usage
column7:
Purchased this one a couple of months back. Have been a Nokia loyalist since more than a decade and just can't convince myself to move over to any other brand. Saw it at a local Nokia store and was immediately taken in by its sleek looks and extremely smooth touch. Here is my unbiased review of the handset.
  

  Pros:
  
  1) Super smooth touch.
  
  2) Brilliant camera quality at 5MP compared to other 5MP cameras in other brands (Micromax, Lenovo, et al).
  
  3) Impressive looks. By default has the Windows Nokia Lumia display in Menu (listed display). But install the app GoLauncher and you get the android grid display in addition to a hoard of other display options.
  
  4) Supports almost all android apps. Download a range of apps from the Nokia store (soon to become Opera android store).
  
  5) Here Maps. This is the best thing about this phone! I am a geographically handicapped guy when it comes to driving as can't remember routes and depend heavily on voice guided instructions. Here Maps works offline without GPRS (you need to pre-download the map for a particular country and state and good to go without data connection).
  
  6) Screen is not gorilla glass, but supposedly scratch resistant. And it totally is scratch resistant. Is a little prone to smudges though - leaves fingerprints n all, but sturdy.
  
  7) Games etc run great. Haven't seen the phone hang even once in the two months, considering I am a heavy user of the phone.
  

  Cons:
  
  1) The biggest con for me is that I could not find any option for downloading whatsapp images/videos etc into the external memory card. Goes by default into the phone ROM (4GB). Same goes with apps. You will need to download the filemanager app from store and do this manually if needed. If anyone is aware of a way of doing it otherwise, please let me know.
  
  2) There is no option in the music player to search for songs. Even older handsets like the E series had this, where you could type a song name in your list and it would come up. X2 doesn't have that. You'll need to scroll through the list to find the song you want to listen to.
  

  For me, the pros totally overshadow the cons though. Taking into account the Nokia trust factor and the rock solid hardware quality we are used to from Nokia handsets, this one in my opinion totally leaves handsets in this price range from other brands way behind.

UPDATE: I bought those earlier two phones from a different Indian ecommerce web site. I had paid approximately INR 1800.00 per phone. But, when I found deeply discounted prices (almost 200 less) at Flipkart, I picked up two more as gifts to people I know would appreciate a great, simple, functional mobile phone. :)
  

  ORIGINAL REVIEW:
  

  In India we often say "practice makes perfect". In Nokia's case, this mobile phone proves that quotable-quote to be true.
  
  Nokia has been making mobile phones for as long as most of us can remember. And I have known a lot of Nokia mobile phone fans. But, I could NEVER become a fan of Nokia mobile phones for various reasons: either they were ugly in looks or ran pathetically bloated software with tons of unnecessary features.
  
  But, as Nokia exits the mobile phone segment (or so I have heard) ... they drop this neat little phone onto the market ... and I feel this phone deserves a million-stars commendation.
  
  What is this phone all about? It's an absolutely basic mobile phone with which you can make/receive calls and send/receive text messages. That's it! That's all it does. Yes, there's a calendar. Yes, there's reminders!! Yes, there's an alarm clock. Yes, there's a super tiny (and possibly useless) flash light. But, that's all there is to it.
  
  Somebody at Nokia still thought it was a bright idea to include a "video" player, but, that fallacy can be ignored. Using this phone for playing videos would be "degrading" it from what it is: a superb, basic mobile phone.
  
  Oh! Did I tell you it accepts an SD card on you can stuff some music on to it and then listen to your music whenever you want? Remember the time when we bought super costly iPods to listen to music? Yeah? This phone makes us look super dumb!!
  
  Did I mention this phone also has an FM radio, if anyone listens to "fm radio" anymore?
  
  But that video player, audio player and FM radio are features I don't care about.
  
  There's NO camera, so you don't have to worry about grainy pictures.
  
  There's NO "internet" and NO web browser on this phone so you don't get frustrated with 1kbps (yes, bits per second) data connections that are charged at sky-high rates.
  

  And the phone is unbelievably small in size and unbelievably light in weight and unbelievably "cute" in looks.
  
  So how did I come to discover it? Mom called ... she wanted to know what's a good phone in the market! She wanted a simple dial pad. No qwerty and definitely no touch screens. And she didn't want any "unnecessary features". So, I looked around and naturally homed onto Nokia. My first choice was Nokia 206. I have it. It's a decent phone but I don't use it. But, after a little thought we concluded the Nokia 206 still had way too many "unnecessary features" in it which mom wouldn't need/want. The Nokia 105 was my second choice, but that was quickly ruled as for "not being elegant". Next in line were Nokia 200 and 225 (or some such models), but I ruled them out because they still had too many "unnecessary features" built in. And then we found this: Nokia 130. Looks elegant. Has just enough features and almost no "unnecessary features" if you ignore the video/audio players. It was light weight. And the price was unbeatable!
  
  Very quickly 2 of the same kind were ordered. One was shipped to mom, the other was kept with me so I can play "phone support" for her if she ever needed any help. She didn't! :)
  
  Personally, I have been using this phone for the past week or two. And I couldn't be happier with a mobile phone. This phone is there when I need to make/receive calls. It is there when I need to send/receive text messages. (Yes! This supports T9!!!) And then phone hides in the pocket without making me aware of its existence till I have to make or receive a call or send/recv a text mesg!!
  

  Before we finish this review ... I have found only one flaw: the battery wanes "quite" quickly compared to our Nokia 206. In case of this phone we have to charge it at least once in 2 days and sometimes more often. But it has a regular micro USB charger, so you can use a regular USB cable to charge the phone off of the computer. And yes, you can mount the phone's SD card to copy/move files from/to it! How cool is that?
  
  To conclude: Super cute, super neat phone. Highly, highly recommended. Would give it a "million stars" if I could.

The phone from its first look is dazzling and well built but as of features it really sucks.
  
  if you are buying this for older people for basic calling go for it without a thought as battery life is awesome, but if you have ever used a smartphone or even an older nokia feature phone or Nseries, under 2 days u will get to know that this sucks.
  
  camera is ok but dont expect much
  
  Cons of the Software:-
  
  You cant add two no.s or address or email in the contact.
  
  There are literally just 4 apps in the app store
  
  As the operating System is MediaTek based(mre) you have nowhere to go for apps unlike Symbian or java
  
  The Opera store has no apps just ads.
  
  You can't install whatsapp no matter how hard you try to find one.
  
  the opera browser( the only browser) is a real bad browser. can't download anything more than 8 mb with confidence that it will surely be downloaded. no tabbed browsing, no uc browser(a great help in java phones)
  
  Music Player is very bad, no playlist or albums just straight all of the songs in front of you
  
  Conclusion:
  
  Buy it if you just are going to just call, but if you are a student trying to just do basic work or google, even then get ready for a long frustration journey.

My experience with the Nokia Lumia 530 DS powered by the Windows Phone 8.1 is going really good. I am glad that I made the choice, not that it was too to make the choice either since it came with a very impressive list of features and functions and that too for a very good price as well. The Nokia Lumia 530 dual sim smartphone has all the attributes of a dual sim handset as well as that of the smartphone as well. I can enjoy the benefits of using two sim on one phone with the call forwarding and call holding options between the two. It has the most amazing apps loaded on it and I am very pleased to find apps like the MS Office which is of a great use to me as I can now do my work even on my phone, the Instagram Beta where I can edit the pictures the I take with the 5 MP camera and even the ones I download as well and also the Nokia HERE Maps which has been successfully guiding me through all the roads and lanes in the city ever since I started using it. Apps like the Nokia Mix Radio and the Shazam are music oriented app and I was delighted to find these unique apps on my phone as well since I am great music lover. I was skeptic at first as I thought so many apps would slow down the system, but I was wrong. The Quad core processor and the 512 MB RAM is responsible for the undisrupted and the smooth functioning of the handset. Also the 1430 mAh capacitated battery is commendable for allowing my phone to run throughout the day without putting it on charge frequently. The Word Flow keypad too is a delight as I can type amazingly fast on it. All the quick settings and the notifications can be found on the Action Centre that can be accessed with one quick swipe.

People complaining about this being a waste of money.
  
  Firstly the price was high at the time of launch. That is the case with every new product.
  
  Now it has been priced reasonably.
  

  Few reasons the price is higher that Lumia 720:
  
   Full HD (1080p) video recording on Lumia 625 as opposed to HD (720p) on Lumia 720.
  
   PureMotion screen with 60Hz refresh rate (found otherwise only on the 920,925 and 1020). (It does lack ClearBlack display though. And also Glance Screen feature isn't supported.)
  
   Nokia Music subscription is for 6 months with Lumia 625 and 3 months on Lumia 720.
  
   Lumia 625 is 4G ready, Lumia 720 supports only 3.5G at the most.
  
   Lumia 625 has a faster processor (1.2ghz dual-core) than Lumia 720 (1ghz dual-core). This results in smoother overall performance.
  
   Lumia 625 comes with Nokia Amber update pre-installed and BlueTooth 4.0 pre-enabled.
  
   (Most obvious point) the screen on Lumia 625 is larger than that on Lumia 720.
  

  And yes, Lumia 625 has FM radio. Some people have wrong info.
  

  Yes, the Lumia 720 has better cameras and supports wireless charging, but you need to understand that a product can only provide you so much in the price you pay for it. And no product is perfect. I have been using this phone since a month now and have fallen in love with it.
  
  I have used an android device for 2 years and now when I planned to get a new one, I was kind of inclined towards a window phone to get a different taste.
  
  My budget was around 15K, my basic requirements were good look, large screen, front camera, good surfing speed.
  
  It took me around 2 weeks to choose between all the phones in this price range, it was tough :-/.
  
  I have this kind of thinking that when I am spending as much as 15k bucks for a phone, I will prefer spending it on brands like Nokia/ Samsung/ HTC or Sony. So in this way my options already got a bit filtered.
  
  Before making this purchase from flipkart, I personally went to a Mobile store to see how these devices actually look in my hand as the outlook of the mobile was one of my major criterion and the Nokia lumia 625 absolutely nailed in it.
  
  Lumia 720 was also a good phone with better camera and "clear black display" but I liked the look of 625 far more because of its larger screen and rounded edge which looked sexy. It doesn't look like a 15k phone, rather having a first sight of the phone and seeing the "Nokia" name on it, one would easily presume that its atleast 23k phone.(I have personally experienced it). I got the Orange colour and it looks just LOVELY! It looks very vibrant! You also have the option to get shells of other colours such as green, black or yellow. I think it will be wiser to go for a black coloured one and then buy an orange shell, coz the price of a black shell is 1200/- online whereas that of a orange shell is around 700/-. So that way you can save your 500/- ;)
  
  I am not going to mention the specs in detail as flipkart has already done that... and trust me, they are not lying :P.
  

  As per my experience with this beautiful device, the pros are:
  
  * Great look, Great build, Superb design, Awfully slim :O.
  
  * Really Large screen. Big enough to clearly surf internet, read books or watch movies. You don't actually need bigger screen than this for a mobile. Else it gets difficult to handle..
  
  * As they say, this phone is 4g ready, therefore when you are using 3g connection, surfing is lightning fast, you will love it.
  
  * The touch of the phone is superb. I can easily handle it even wearing hand gloves.
  
  * You will love the interface of Window 8, if you are a first time user.
  
  * The camera is real good. I don't think, you buy a camera mobile to be a professional photographer or so. For that you have to go for expensive cameras from sony/nikon blah blah. In a 15k camera mobile you expect a decent camera which captures clear and decent quality image. Lumia 625 serves you very well in this category. The flash is also very good. The low light images are also good. Not as good as the day light images though.
  
  * HD Video recording. this is a real good feature of this phone. When you see the videos in your laptop, its real pleasure.
  
  * I don't generally rely on headphones given free with the device. i use my Sennheiser headphones with this device and It works just fine. I love the sound quality.
  
  * The Speaker is good, real loud and clear.
  
  * Battery back up is another great thing of this wonderful device. You charge it full, You use it for a whole 10-12 hrs, playing games, listening songs, surfing nets, which was like a dream when I used to have an android device.
  
  * Window phone doesn't hang. Processing speed is fast.
  
  * With this phone you get 6 months unlimited subscription of songs from Nokia Music and  movies from Nokia movies which is also great.
  
  * In the Nokia mix radio, you will find good varieties of mixes of various genres and artists.
  
  * There are almost every kind of apps you need in the store.
  
  * The gorilla glass looks awesome on the mobile. You will not feel the need to spend your money on buying a scratch guard for it seriously.
  

  Cons if you want me to tell: :-/
  
  * People will point out the absence of clear black display in this category. But I don't find it difficult to read the screen even under the sun.
  
  * Its 480x800 Pixels resolution. Its actually a bit down for a screen size of 4.7". But the thing is, it actually doesn't harm the display. You choose bright coloured tiles and increase the brightness, it ill do. So don't worry! :)
  
  * In the store, I find most of high end games are paid. For example I got the "real football" game free in my previous android mobile but in windows 8 store, you have to pay to get it.
  
  However its not really a con for me, as I am not into much gaming. Still if you are a gamer, the large screen will serve well for you ;).
  
  That's all I had to say after using this for a month. Lumia 625 is definitely a very good buy!
  

  A small tip: Go through the detailed specs of the mobiles whatever you choose before buying it. I do get surprised when I see people saying in the review "this phone has only 5 mp camera...this phone has low resolution...this phone has only 512mb ram..blah blah!!!" You should have known this facts before buying it!

column6: Passionate about Smartphones? Check out the Nokia Lumia 625
column7:
Are you passionate about Smartphones? If so, you must check out the latest carriage of the Lumia train, the powerful Nokia Lumia 625. I think it is one of the best Smartphones that I have managed to purchase and am reasonably satisfied by its performance. It has certainly helped me in the realisation of my passion and I am sure you will have to say the same after using it.
  
  Labelled as a mid range phone, although for me it is no less than a 'high end' phone, the Nokia Lumia 625 stands tall and committed. It is dedicated to the breed of users who are extremely passionate about innovative gadgets; so it runs on the right track for me. The phone succeeds in carving a niche for itself among the mushrooming number of Smartphones that inundate the electronic market with and makes the user feel indulged and transformed.
  
  The Smartphone features a platform that is a hot favourite and at par with top Android phones. As I can gather, you will find a lot of things better and customisable with the Windows Phone 8. The best part is, it is upgradeable and rest assured you will never fall behind. The capacitive touchscreen, I feel, is way more effective than resistive touchscreens.
  
  The phone has the common Lumia design with monoblock touch as its form factor, smooth curves on the edges, and Corning Gorilla Glass 2 and polycarbonate panel adorning its body. The display at 4.7 inches is wonderfully big and adjustable, and equipped with various sensors and outdoor viewing enhancements.
  
  Nokia Lumia 625's 5 MP camera acts as a good camera substitute for those who wish to take some decent click here and there but without shelling out money on a separate photographic device. It has many features common to a good quality digicam, e.g., auto focus with two-stage capture key, a 28 mm focal length, f/2.4 f-number/ aperture, LED flash, HD video recording and panorama lens to name a few. Also on the offing is an app that lets you shoot a sequence of photos to choose the one that best suits your fancy and even make a strobe effect. Besides, the phone's vast storage capacity helps me store every thing I download, create or work on and eliminates the requirement of clearing up space every other day.
  
  Thanks to the phone's additional set of features which includes Dolby sound, listening to songs on the phone is not only agreeable but also very pleasant. The presence of GPRS, EDGE, WLAN, Bluetooth and a USB port calls for undisturbed sharing of data and other multimedia files. That is not all. There's Here Maps to let the wanderer in you explore the horizons of the earth and guide you to your destination till you have reached.
  
  To cut the long story short, the functions of the Nokia Lumia 625 along with the extras make it unique and a Smartphone worth recommending. All credit goes to the Finnish company for relentlessly working on breaking newer grounds.

We purchased Nokia Lumia 625 2 weeks back from local store and here is the feedback:
  

  We earlier had Android (HTC wildfire S), and decided to switch to Lumia for some thing different and now regretting our decision. Lets start with Cons:
  

  Cons:
  
  1> Call alert:
  
  You need extra sensitive ear and skin to realize incoming call.
  
  a> On Vibration mode - Its Vibration is extremely poor.
  
  b> On Ring+Vibration mode - it Vibrate only once (sick) and then rings. You should have God gifted ears (like Krishh) to hear the ring.
  
  c> To make the matter worse, its speaker is placed at lower back, and gets covered very easily to make the ring difficult if not impossible to be audible.
  
  d> Result - maximum incoming calls are missed.
  
  2> What's app:
  
  a> What's app behaves like a drunkard. It exist frequently without asked to do so. :(
  
  b> While drafing What's-app chat - Android Mobile displays the profile photo of the receipient along with name; but Lumia shows only Name. Click on name to see the profile photo.
  
  c> Font placing and emoticons are not impressive
  
  3> Calls:
  
  a> Speaker phone is clear but very mild. (not impressive, Wildfire S was far better)
  
  4> Contact transfer:
  
  a> Like Android needs Gmail account, Lumia needs Hotmail account. So create an account first.
  
  b> While transferring contact from Android to Lumia (Bluetooth transfer) transfer doesn't take place smoothly. Eg. If a contact have 2 mobile and 1 email id in Android, while transferring to Lumia, it gets 3 different contact ID, now take the pain to link them.
  
  5> Display:
  
  a> Display is large enough that you can read from 5 Feets :D and still the font size is small. Note that it has 400x800 resolution.
  
  6> Computer connectivity:
  
  a> Connecting to computer is big pain. Its not easy like Android.
  
  b> Lumia can not be used as extended Flash drive to PC. You need different software to connect it to PC. I remember, in my old android, i use to connect it to PC and fetch photos and videos via USB cable, but with Nokia life is very complicated. I am yet to figure out, how to connect it to PC. Though I have downloaded 100mb software - Zune, but still its not giving desired result.
  

  Pros:
  
  1> There is a feature to double tap on screen to wake-up the screen. No need to hunt for the button to wake-up the screen.
  
  2> Its desktop is conveniently customizable
  
  3> Camera and music is good
  
  4> It gives unlimited access to not so large database of music. (good to have but not impressive)
  
  5> It also give 90 days access to 3000 movies but all old (like DDLJ, Ek tha Tiger kind...). Its not latest. I tried some Hollywood movies but not all are free. (Waste)
  
  6> Battery is good
  
  7> Store - Import apps are available on Store, but have limited variety/ stock. Android collection is far more dynamic and huge then Lumia Store. (not impressive)
  

  To summarize, i will say - you buy phone and rest all are its features. But with low ringer and vibration (google it... this is global issue) it defeats the basic purpose of having a mobile.
  
  You can go if this issue is not important, but in that case there are Tabs (with call and without call feature) in market.
  

  Personally, I will NOT recommend LUMIA to any of my friends and family members.
  

  -regards,
  
  Tarun

column6: I bought this phone and has been using it for a week now. Read on:
column7:
Absolutely unusable in bed, the corners prick my had when I try to type, and Windows Phone 8 doesn't let me turn off screen rotation which is a pain (hope this comes in a further update)!
  

  The phone is built rock solid and feels very premium, my brother has a SGS3 and comparatively my 920 is much better.
  

  The brightness can be adjusted to only three levels, low, medium and high. With low still being pretty bright. Auto Brightness works like a charm and brings brightness to a much lower level than the default "low" setting, but I wish I could have done that manually so as to conserve my battery.
  

  Battery lasts a day if used judiciously. It was very average for the first two days, which disappointed me, but it improved drastically after a couple of full charges and discharges! :O
  

  Nokia Music, Nokia Maps and Nokia City Lens. Damn!! Love these. And also the fact that I get a free subscription to Nokia Music for an year (legal, hq music) gets me every time. It even has Malayalam and Tamil music apart from Hindi and World.
  

  I can download attachments from email but I do not know where it gets stored, which means that I cannot delete them manually. They get deleted automatically as and when the email gets deleted from my inbox (sync settings allow you to sync email from the past 3 days, past 7 days, past 2 weeks and any time).
  

  There isn't a file manager which lets me browse through the files on my phone. You cannot find one on the Windows Marketplace either.
  

  But of course, you can drag and drop files to and from your pc which makes transferring songs and videos between my phone and pc very easy.

Nokia being on its last legs has decided to go all out on their Lumia series with the hope of capturing the early glories of its hey day. Guess what, it shows through on their phones, be it ergonomics, design, style or application.
  

  When you switch on the phone, the first thing that strikes you is the innovative and beautifully designed tiles that sets it apart from any of its competitors. Combine that along with the option of changing the tile colors, size and look, you've got the freedom of customizing to suit your needs. Don't get me started on the resolution. It easily is above the Iphone 5 or Samsung S3. The tiles are constantly changing and when you play a track on the phone, the music tile scrolls the name of the song and the artist. Certain apps like dictionary (free) keeps changing and the last viewed word is constantly on the tile. This helps believe in learning one word a day. Small changes like these make this a very practical phone.
  

  The phone is also extremely user friendly and offers many small but innovative changes that make the phone such a joy to use. Almost anything (contacts, videos, photos, apps, individual tracks etc) can be "pinned" to the main screen for easy access. This has made my life a lot easier and can help in quickly accessing things that I often use. The best part about this phone is its multi tasking ability. I have often opened 5 or 6 different windows (application, contacts, music, messaging) at the same time and holding the back button for a second shrinks all the windows "mac style" and the desired window can immediately be accessed without losing the current window. Even when multiple windows are opened (5 -6), the phone never slows down.
  

  The nokia app store, though not as diverse and loaded like the Apple store, still provides a lot of useful applications. Nokia Maps provides the option of downloading a map of any country and can be accessed offline. This is such a blessing when I need directions and don't have good internet connection. Nokia Music provides 1 year of unlimited subscription and can be used to download albums free of cost.
  

  As far as practicality goes, this phone is right there at the top. I have used IOS for the last 4 years and I found the transition from Apple to Nokia seamless. The contact list is alphabetically arranged and the tile can be clicked on to bring about the entire alphabet list to quickly navigate to the desired contact. While the Iphone has the closely packed side bars which quite often misses the correct input and takes me either to the preceding or the succeeding alphabet.
  

  The entire history of a contact can be accessed either through the calls list or the contact list (swiping either side will lead to the entire message thread, photo album, facebook, mail etc of the contact). Such small changes make a huge difference when using the phone. The only gripe I have with this phone is the absence of customized labels which IOS provides. you are presented only with generic contacts titles (home 1, office 1 etc) which leads to confusion especially when you have friends who use 2 or 3 phones.
  

  The camera is one of the key features of the phone and has one of the best low light performance of any phone on the market today. Being a photographer, I can confidently say that this phone is a solidwhen it comes to capturing photos with very little light and its low light performance is very well ahead of any phone. for the geeks, the camera goes upto ISO 800.
  

  There is so much to be said about this phone but I there is nothing like the joy of discovery. I am not a Nokia fanboy (the last nokia phone I had was the 7610 way back in 2006). I have been waiting for quite sometime to buy this phone since it was introduced and I am glad. The phone has exceeded my best expectations.
  

  Pro's:
  
  Excellent ergonomics
  
  Beautifully designed
  
  The screen resolution is simply amazing
  
  Hugely customizable
  
  practical
  
  Very good camera
  
  Small innovative tweaks that go a long way
  

  Cons:
  
  No customizable contact label
  
  32gb with no external memory slot
  
  Slightly big (but you'll get over it soon once you see its resolution and the quality)
  
  limited app store
  

  For those of you who are saving up for a smart phone, go ahead and buy this phone without a thought, you'll love it. Everyone (friends, family) who've seen this phone have fallen instantly in love with its alluring beauty and once I've given them a taste of what this phone can do, they are hooked. These are guys who used Iphone's and Samsung for years. Nokia is back with the same innovative mindset that helped them establish a monopoly on the mobile market in India over a decade ago.
  

  I very rarely post reviews of products I have purchased and I decided to post this because I am bit partial to Nokia (my first phone was a Nokia) and hope this review convinces someone to buy this brilliant phone that may otherwise be buried under the over saturated, big brand name market of the smart phone

column6: Myths and facts about windows phone 8 and nokia lumia 920
column7:

  quad core in samsung galaxy s3 is better than daul core in lumia 920
  

  fact:

  windows phone 8 does not support bluetooth file transfers and it needs zune to transfer songs or videos or pictures.

  WINDOWS PHONE 7 has these limitations but not windows phone 8. column6: Why I would personally NOT RECOMMEND it wholeheartedly - though BRILLIANT PHONE
column7:
I'm a student of SciTech and I wanted a phone that would simplify my life by reducing the number of things I carry around in my pocket: to merge a phone with good reception, a great camera (can sneakily take great pictures inside classrooms even!), a mini-tablet that reads, writes, takes notes, translates etc, and easily synchs with my laptop. Also, incredibly durable.
  

  The natural choice was the best phone Nokia could make - from past experience - and luckily, it comes with a great camera.
  

  Am I satisfied? Well, here are the good points:
  

  1)Amazing touch sensitivity (I can navigate with my finger 1mm off the screen) and response - feels great to own
  

  2)good storage 32GB
  

  3)good battery - it only eats the battery when you are playing games, but performs reasonably well with movies and you can hear songs on it all day. Internet surfing time is pretty decent. Overnight, it was connected to wifi and updated all apps- I have a lot of apps - and synched facebook and gmail - after 24hrs it had lost 1% battery... brilliant!
  

  4) Very decent camera with good apps (look up Nokia Lenses). Android may have more variety though but then, the quality of images is brilliant only on the 920 overall, if you consider image resolution, quality, and stabilization. There is a button for camera and the camera can be accessed even when the screen is locked with a long press of the button - I don't know how many of you will appreciate the importance of this.
  

  5) I like the tiles - life is a lot more simpler, but miss the Live-wallpaper on Androids (not like I used it anyway, to conserve battery!) The interface is very simplified and nothing really is missing, unless you are a hellbent on having the Android screens. In fact, there is a nice feature called "hubs" which groups different kinds of apps together, which does look like the Android or iOs shells - but you can't modify it. Still, life is simpler - the pre-programmed grouping is convenient.
  

  6) I know the apps are terribly incompetent compared to Android but face it - the growth curve is sharper for WP8. I like the apps (but most of the good ones are not free, so beware). Most of the ones important to me are there. The Nokia specific apps are cool especially Cityscape. So dont get very worried that WP8 is primitive compared to Andrd and iOs (read: 10 Windows Phone 8 Features That Would Make Android Even Sweeter by Kavafian)
  

  7) Synchs pretty well with Windows7
  

  8) Looks beautiful, looks amazing (I have Matte black), is very strong and it's a little heavy but unlike what I feared - you don't feel the weight, even in your pocket. It's about 50-60g heavier than what most people are used to. Cmon, that's seriously not much!
  

  Some drawbacks.
  

  1) Non-removable battery, so you cannot carry a spare one around.
  
  2) Heats up randomly - while wirelessly charging, while playing for some while...
  
  These are synonymous with those of other highend, heavyduty smartphones also. We've been reduced to people who need to charge everyday and have started calling a good battery one which sees you through an entire day. Well, if you aren't gaming, LM920 is good in that respect, but an hour idling away playing games is a serious issue - eats up 20-30%!
  

  3) ONE TERRIBLE SHORTAGE...
  
  There is no ****** document manager. Sure it reads your PDF's and after a labourious process, reads your epubs also, but what sucks is that you cannot manage all these in folders! So if you are like me - this means scrolling through about 4000 files in one list (haven't uploaded them yet for this precise reason). I would really like a folder system - WP8 DEVELOPPERS DO SOMETHING!This is why I would not recommend a WP8, not just the Lumia 920.
  

  So am I in love with LM920? Yes! But given a chance to get the money back and invest in a different phone (like Samsung Note2?) would I do it? Yes. Definitely. This is because I REALLY MISS the folder system and the LM920 is making life hard here. Although, it's really fancy and will serve me well in parties and travel trips (as long as I carry a charger). So yeah, if you don't really care about these cons - LM920 IS the phone you want.

column6: Some good, some not so good. Solid product, overall.
column7:
Posting in list format about features I can think of.
  

  -Phone  build quality- Superb (was there any doubt?). If you can live with the size, it feels awesome.
  

  -Call Quality- Also outstanding
  

  -User Interface- It's different, but nothing worrying, has a very short learning curve and once one gets used to it feels just as good as any competing platform. It's really a matter of personal choice on this one, and IMO, Is not a positive or negative aspect, unless it's overly cumbersome. What is good though is the fluidity of the UI in all regions. Again, that's nothing to boast about now, because competing platforms are at par too.
  

  -Apps- The situation is not as dire as nay- sayers would like to have us believe, but let's face it, it isn't exactly brimming with apps either. I see this as a very temporary issue though, because with MSFT pouring money into the platform, there is a noticeable forward push. There are all the core apps one could need and plenty more are incoming. The down side is the market interface itself. While it works perfectly and is informative enough,  a little more data, like on Android would be good, like total number of downloads, version rating and rating for your device. That having been said, it's still decent and no where near as bad as people who get emotionally invested in a company or product, because they bought it (don't want to call them fanboys/ girls) like to believe.
  

  -Multitasking- This is the one semi downside to this platform. It works for core apps, and WP has had it since Mango (WP7.5), but for some reason a lot of developers have not been able to make use of it. I can live with it, but I'm not really pleased with it as it is. I'm only hoping that at some stage, it gets pushed a little more to at least iOS levels.
  

  Camera- LOL, I was saving this for last, but then I realised that pretty much anything that had to be said has been said in countless reviews on the web. To sum it up, awesome low light stills and daylight/ low light video, not so outstanding, while still decent, stills in good light. The only thing I have to add, is that while the portico update was supposed to fix the blur, it hasn't completely achieved its goal. Check DP Reviews on that because for photography related reviews, that's where one goes, and not to tech sites which carry on their brand of fanboy journalism/ blogging.
  

  Outright negative aspects are
  
  -No core time suite (countdown timer/ stopwatch) app, Timers sometimes fail to buzz in the background or outright quit because the developers didn't code properly. The manufacturer should have provided this as a standard running in conjunction with the phone clock.
  

  -Volume settings get reverted to standard after a reboot and if you forget to push it up/ down, you have a ringer at an undesirable sound level. (I hope they see this as an obvious flaw and fix it.)
  

  Can't really think of much else, and to summarise my impression, I really like this device and am hopeful for the platform. It has a couple of problems, but at this stage in it's life, I think it is ahead of where the competition was.

column6: Switched from Samsung Galaxy S3 to lumia 720 to 920
column7:
I was a Nokia user a long time ago, N8 to 808 and 808 went to my wife and I got the Galaxy s3. Here are the reasons I switched from S3 to Windows Phone Nokia 720 to 920
  
  The 720 got wet in the rain and is beyond repair:(, and then I moved to 920 by selling my Galaxy S3.
  
  The point numbers match b/w the S3 and the 920
  
  1. The phone used to randomly reboot at times
  
  2. After about 100 hours of usage the phone would become very slow I had to reboot
  
  3. Unpredictable Battery life, I like to keep wifi on throughout the day. Suppose you forget to close some app, it drains your battery very quickly
  
  4. UI of the apps is too cluttered You have one big screen with lots of buttons here and there and each app can choose where it can place the buttons. with the huge screens of the S3/4 you have to reach your finger to the button from corner to corner, single handed use is impossible.
  
  5. Notorious apps than can suck your data plan and battery
  
  6. Call drops inside elevators at work (signal boosters installed in work place)
  
  7. lousy and pics/videos on the camera
  

  After switching to lumia
  
  1. Excellent Stablity, I don't know when my phone rebooted or when I rebooted, Reboots only when I run out of juice, which is again rare.
  
  2. excellent standby time. I unplug in the night and leave the phone on (wifi and mobile data shutoff) it is still 100 % in the morning. I use GPS tracking for 30 mins when I cycle to work, I reach office and it still is at 100 %!! that is insane. I never turn off GPS
  
  3. Windows phone, the OS has this thing called freeze, it shuts down apps that are not in background if there is no activity, that way even if I leave an app running It does not drain battery.
  
  4. Excellent UI and always predictable know where the menu's are located, and a simple swipe to right or left will get the job done. I always like the single handed use of the lumia 720, 920 is a bit large but I can still manage.
  
  5. Apps are not much, but more than enough for me, what ever apps are available they behave correctly and integrate well with the OS. MS has been doing some strict monitoring.
  
  6. I have not had a single call drop in elevators at work. If there is no signal, well nothing can be done about that, phone indicates that there is no signal.
  
  7. Excellent pics and Videos, I have the latest firmware, the older firmware had issues with colours and daylight photography. I get Excellent indoor shots as good as some compact cameras
  

  I am a power user, I have configured 4 email ID's on the phone, my work email is set sync as the mail arrives all other email sync every hour, facebook, google contacts, I have about 10 games, I play about 15 to 30 mins daily. I mainly use for facebook and email. sometimes Youtube. MS took the you-tube app off :(
  
  I am impressed with the phone,
  
  The only thing nagging me is the Volume control, the Volume control from speaker and headphone is the same :( It is the stupidest thing in the phone. I hope it gets fixed in the upcoming update from MS.
  
  BTW I did not buy the phone from flipkart.

Multi-tasking is also amazing. (If you didn't know that windows OS has multi-tasking option, then you need to google it). Phone is superfast and screen transition is extra smooth. Data transfer between phone and PC is also fast.
  

  2. Storage: I am a kind of guy who doesn't want to be bothered by storage concerns. 32GB is too much. You won't ever have hassle of inserting memory card in your phone ( as it doesn't have memory slot, but 32 GB is more than enough).
  

  3. Music: Nokia always provides best music experience and this is no exception. Add to that Xbox Music from windows and it's a deadly combo.
  

  4. Camera: Camera is pretty amazing with Carl Zeiss lens. No one can beat this phone in low light photography. Camera app is not that evolved but I am sure we will have more features soon.
  

  5. Nokia Maps: Nokia Maps is the feature which wins my heart. Once you download the map, you don't need to connect to data network. Just switch on GPS and you can use every feature of map (navigation, places etc). Android phones simply can't provide this.
  

  6. Apps: Windows app store is not as developed as android's and apple's, but you will find all popular apps you need. If you are game junky, then Xbox has pretty amazing games.
  

  7. Microsoft Office: If you need to work with Microsoft Office as part of your job, then you can mobile work using this phone. And the best thing is seamless integration with PC and Sky Drive comes pretty helpful too.

Having used a variety of smartphones, I was a bit sceptical when I heard Nokia had launched its own series of Lumia smartphones. The brand has been an icon of reliability, but for some apparent reason, had fallen behind its competitors when it came to smartphones. But, when I could not resist the allure and got my hands on the Nokia Lumia 920, I was in for a real surprise. This smartphone is surely one of the most innovative devices to be ever launched by Nokia.
  

  The unibody polycarbonate design of my Lumia 920 is not like anything I have seen yet, and it comes in such vibrantly coloured covers. The camera on my new Nokia smartphone is a whopping 8.7 MP rear shooter that comes with a cutting-edge and sophisticated Carl Zeiss Tessar lens. Integrating PureView camera technology and optical image stabilisation, this camera renders all my photographs in pristine quality, almost as if shot by a professional photographer. Also included, is a dual LED flash that lights up the night and allows low-light imaging.
  

  The screen of my Lumia 920 is a 4.5-inch LCD touch display that features PureMotion HD+ technology. It responds quickly to my touch and can also be used when wearing gloves. The curved design of the display provides enhanced readability in direct sunlight. With Corning Gorilla Glass 2 protection, this tough display easily weathers my rough use. The Windows Phone 8 operating system in my Lumia 920 is a breakthrough in terms of convenience and navigation. It comes with features like PeopleHub that helps me tag all my frequently used contacts to my home screen. All their social networking updates reach me directly, without the effort of logging into these sites and browsing to their profiles. The Live Tiles interface lets me arrange all my frequently used apps and games on my home screen. Microsoft Office comes pre-installed on my phone and the support for MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint make work on the move, really simple and enjoyable. I also use the integrated MS Outlook app for managing my emails.
  

  My Lumia 920 outperforms quite a few of its contemporaries due to its dual core 1.5 GHz GHz Qualcomm Snapdragon S4 'Krait' mobile processor, an Adreno 225 graphics chip and 1 GB RAM. This makes multitasking a breeze and lets me play HD games and execute memory-intensive apps. Storing data is also not a problem, as I can use the 32 GB onboard memory. Additionally, Nokia also provides complimentary SkyDrive storage for additional data needs.
  

  When on the move, I do not like to ask for directions to my destination. This is where the Nokia Maps and Nokia Drive apps of my Lumia 920 come in handy. They provide me with turn by turn directions even when I am not subscribed to data usage. On the connectivity front, my Lumia 920 comes with Wi-Fi, WLAN, NFC and Bluetooth which makes exchanging files and accessing the web all the more easy.

I bought a Lumia 920 in March 2013 from The Mobile Store Gurgaon at INR 37000, and just within 4 days of buying it, the phone crashed. The phone would just hang up whenever I started the camera and only a hard reset could bring the phone back. I went to the local Nokia Care and they said it will be repaired. I requested a replacement and I was turned down. Then I wrote to Stephen Elop, then CEO of Nokia about this and within 4 days I got a brand new piece. I was grateful about the prompt customer care experience.
  

  I still faced hang-ups whenever I would use Here Maps and Here applications. But in the meantime, my sim got disconnected and I could not test this further. For about an year, I used this mobile only for photos, music and data storing/editing. Here too I wrote a mail to Stephen Elop, but I guess by then my emails may have been tagged as spam in Stephen's inbox.
  

  After I was transferred to Pune, in July 2014, I bought a new sim and the hang-up issues resurfaced. One fine day, after 2 hours of charging, the screen stopped working. I again went to the local Nokia Care and they said that the screen needs to be replaced and I will be charged INR 13500 for the same because my phone's warranty expired in May 2014.
  

  This time too I wrote to Stephen Elop, and this time too no response from him. Instead I got a response from India Repair Manager that they will provide me concession and I will have to pay INR 8200 + Taxes. I requested to know the reason for this failure even after handling the mobile as delicately as possible, but nobody cared to respond on that. Instead I got a follow-up email asking my opinion about the concession provided.
  

  I was a fan of Nokia and that is the reason I have bought 3 Nokia phones till date viz. 3315, X6 and Lumia 920. I have also used Motorola, Blackberry, Micromax, Ericsson, and all of these phones are still working including X6 and 3315. But Lumia 920 has turned out to be the worst mobile I have ever used even after it being a smartphone. And on top of that, the customer care experience has been so GOOD (sarcastically), that I would recommend a Noble Prize for Nokia Customer Care.

column6: Decent hardware with not so good OS
column7:
Hi all,
  
  First of all I gave this product 2 stars based purely on my personal experience with this phone for 6 months (i would like to mention that I am a heavy user of smartphones), so Lumia lovers - no hard feelings.
  

  Prior to owning this phone, i used S3 and I was totally in love with it, I am not going to write about my experience with it here though. I lost it in an accident and was in search of a worthy successor and after lot of research and to satisfy my itch to try new platform, I bought this phone and from day one I absolutely hate it. Here are my reasons:
  

  Interface:
  
  MS has made WP8 very intutively and also been successful in creating an almost crash free OS, no doubt about that. But, doing this, they have made the OS so light that interface looks boring (tiles-many of you might like this but I dont).
  
  Also, doing anything in this phone is not as easy as in an android phone like switching on/off the bluetooth, GPS, WIFI, mobile data, flight mode etc etc.. For everthing I need to go to settings and navigate from there
  
  If I am in an application like Gmaps or watching videos and then I receive a message, I need to exit to main screen open the mesage app and then see the message. Just a swiping for notification will do the job in android.
  

  Battery icon, network strength, bluetooth/wifi status etc are shown at the top of the screen, which is good, but why the hell they are hidden all the time? This phone wont notify me untill the battery gets critically low and the I have to run for charging point. Also if i forget to swith wifi/mobile data/bluetooth off, i should be able to see something on the screen which will notify me that they are still on, if they are hidden, i would not know their status.
  

  Sharing
  
  Everytime I want to share a pic, i need to go to home screen , then go to settings, open the bluetooth and switch it on and go back all the way and then share the pic. If bluetooth is off, then "bluetooth" wont show up in the sharing list and it would not ask me if i want to switch it on or not. Android will ask let me know if bluetooth is off and ask me if i would like to switch it on or not.
  

  lockscreen:
  
  Android shows every notification related every app installed in the phone in lock screen when it is locked. But I have to bloody choose from the list of apps in my phone in lumia and thats all, it wont show the notifications for which i have not selected.
  

  Internet explorer
  
  I dont think I should write much about this as all of you know about it.
  

  Media
  
  Nokia Music is one of the two reasons why I choose to give 2 stars for this phone. Musicis absolutely mind blowing and the dolby make it one of the best in the market. And 1 year free subscription is a boon and the app is absolutely stunning.
  

  Video watching is great but there are some irritating points here like the screen ans capacitive buttons are always active. If i touch anyone of them, it responds and navigates away from the video. If I try to lock the phone, the whole phone is locked stopping the video. Android phones lock the phone and the screen but leave the video on. Even if i accedentally touch the screen or the capacitive buttons, it shows that the phone is locked, how cool is that?
  

  Hardware
  
  This is where it earns another star from me, its just astounding. its rock solid and screen is great, camera is next to god and designe is amazing. I totally love the hardware, I wish android were there in the phone instead of WP8
  

  Finally, I think I made a biggest mistake of my like buying this phone, i feel like this because may be because I came from android platform. I strongly think that people who love this phone are from IOS platform or new to smartphone world or haven't used android properly. My suggestion - DO NOT BUY!!!!

column6: Bright Yellow Workhorse with some low points
column7:
Purchase:
  
  Superb order booking, tracking to delivery a day before committed time from Flipkart and the seller WSRetail, unbeatable price, fantastic support on queries upto and after the delivery. The feedback is post usage and monitoring of about 3 weeks now.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Phone Box is pretty neat nifty handy box if needed to carry in car. The charging cable and headphone are put in the plastic round sleeves which seem like a very nice way of carrying them around in pocket instead squeezing it bare in pocket.
  
  2. Was skeptical about the Yellow color. Went for Yellow instead of White and really fell for the color after getting it in hand. It is quite subjective though to once choice. But a superb bright Yellow and it makes stand out, but also out of place amongst business phones especially when at business meetings. However, I have got around liking it even more with use.
  
  3. Really feels rugged and tough, maybe because of its weight too. Also I like weightier (but not excessive) phones which make their presence felt in hand. Still this is nearly palm-sized and can be nicely gripped in hand. Manufacturing is flawless to say the least and definitely makes for an eye candy. Also refer to Cons point on this though.
  
  4. Mistakenly once slid down from about 1.5-2' (not a great height but still) directly onto the tiled floor and absolutely nothing happened. Though, I will not let it fall from higher grounds and specifically have been focusing on not to let it slip again.
  
  5. Screen looks impressive, unbreakable with glass overflowing the design brilliantly. Visibility really good from all angles both insides and outsides in Sun and I have set it use lowest brightness all times, gives out brilliant colors. Screen touch feels nice and Touch UI is extremely responsive.
  
  6. Keys on right side are nicely placed for usability. Camera key is a boon to wakeup camera directly.
  
  7. Dual Speakers are nice, decent for calls and even adequate for a resounding sound to all rooms at higher volumes but could have been better.
  
  8. Headphones are superb, fit snugly in the ear blocking out external sounds and noises. They offer amazing sound quality especially for music.
  
  9. The phone is really fast, opening & switching between apps. Apps is not a big downside for me as most of business features, emails, calls, messaging, office are fantastically integrated alongwith syncing on SkyDrive providing seamless bidirectional OneNote, Docs, Contacts syncing both ways on SkyDrive and Hotmail. WP8 GDR2 has bettered the experience a lot with Data Sense, Storage views, temp storage cleanups etc. Internet Explorer is very fast.
  
  10. Connectivity of WiFi, Bluetooth for headset is pretty good.
  
  11. Thankfully no hung Windows so far, though heard some feedback.
  
  12. Music Player is nice. Playlists of choice can be created using folders at one go in Windows Explorer when connected to laptop.
  
  13. Camera is fantastic, both the main and front, amazing quality of photos and videos though the HD video eats up disk space pretty fast. The low light photos and videos are highlights of the camera and the software.
  
  14. Kids corner is a boon and it works beautifully.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. The shiny smooth polycarbonate body is slithery and prone to slip out from hand and needs a really firm grip sometimes. Matt body finish on all colors would have helped greatly.
  
  2. Speakers though good lack punch when playing music. The superb headphone-like speaker quality could have been possible.
  
  3. Atleast a nice carrying pouch should have been provided as a default accessory if not a flip cover.
  
  4. The Battery life is the biggest sore point for such a fantastic business cum entertainment phone. With nothing, no apps running in foreground or background, no games, no glance and nothing that could eat up battery life consistently, minimal use of telephony, extremely conservative nearly standby life all day long gives barely 12 hours life. Battery profiler sorely required. Battery app I am using has shown weird charging rates at different times, 40-30-15-22-32%/hr and unreasonable discharge speeds of 3-7%/hr when nothing is running at all purely with WiFi, BT, 2G switched ON. The battery charging times are also too high varying from 3-5 hrs. I generally drain complete battery and recharge it.
  
  5. Badly missing BT File Transfer, File Explorer that even my old E72 had. Closing apps is a pain especially Internet Explorer when there are multiple web pages traversed, though individual tab closing is possible by going into tabs and clicking cross. Email deletion deletes it from server directly, there could have been option provided whether to delete or not, instead of deleting it permanently from server.
  
  6. Additional MicroSD slot would have helped greatly.
  
  7. Here Maps need huge improvement to match with Google Maps, are just sufficiently usable.
  

  Overall, I find it a superb business cum entertainment phone only marred by the battery if used heavily for games, maps and internet browsing.

column6: Superb piece of tech with some niggling OS flaws
column7:
I've always loved camera-centric phones and have had my eye on the 920 thanks to the rave reviews about it's camera ever since it's introduction. Unfortunately I have always had a mental block against buying phones above 20k, not to mention, an aversion to touchscreens. My trusty E6 serves me well for my business needs but my back-up N82 (yes, it still works absolutely perfectly) which I used for my second number was straining under the weight of the newer updates of Whatsapp. So when I saw the price drop on Flipkart, I pounced, albeit a little slow because I missed the 20k price and ended up buying it for 21.5k. I was a little disappointed but I understand the logic of demand and supply and let me tell you, the phone was a steal even at this price.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Super smooth response with no lag whatsoever
  
  2. Premium materials
  
  3. Rugged construction
  
  4. I found all the apps I needed for my purposes on the Windows Store. Except Instagram and BBM messenger, obviously; but I have no interest in them so it was irrelevant. I did find something called 6Tag which connects to Instagram but didn't try it.
  
  5. Here Maps isn't at par with Google Maps but I found a 3rd party app that superimposes Google Maps results on the Here Maps and then you can use Drive+ to navigate even if the destination isn't marked on Here Maps. This disadvantage actually becomes a big advantage when you consider the savings on network costs as Nokia maps are stored offline in the memory.
  

  Deal-maker:
  
  Superb camera with OIS and 2-stage hardware shutter key. Much better than poking at the screen. Though, you can still tap to focus and click. Taken some very nice pictures that way. The Panorama mode is accurate and seamless. Low-light photography is simply briliant.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. No notification light. Something that would be expected from a phone that used to the top of the line. You can set notifications from a limited number of apps to appear on the lockscreen.
  
  2. Call forwarding is very basic and the only option is to forward all calls. Even the old Symbian phones had the option to forward if busy, if unanswered or if unavailable. This was very disappointing as I am often in areas where network is weak and my calls need to be diverted to my office if my phone is unreachable. I found a work around online where you can manually send codes to the network operator via the phone keypad and activate the divert you need but this seems like a massive step back. I found only 1 app in the Windows Store that could do this but since I have the codes to do it manually, I didn't bother. Also the app was very low rated. (From what I read in the forums this is a problem with iOS as well though I didn't bother researching that.)
  
  3. No custom keyboards and sadly no Swype.
  
  4. No user-replaceable battery
  
  5. No SD card slot
  

  Conclusion: Money well spent! Still, not a touchscreen fan, so using it as my back-up phone to surf, play games and as a replacement for the ahead-of-it's-time camera of the N82.

I ordered my phone on the 16th. I didn't bother to read the comments then, Got the phone on the 18th, turned it on, felt the vibration but I was surprised to see no Nokia logo on the screen. I simple assumed that phone's battery must have been completely drained and plugged it for charging. I heard the sound but again no battery logo for the next 20 minutes or so. Even the buttons were working and I was even able to take a screenshot. Then I understood that the display was defective.
  

  Called up flipkart with a bit of disappointment since it was the first defective product I received from them. I was told that they would get back to me in a short while. Within 30-40 minutes of me calling, their representative called back. He told me to try a soft reset, I had already tried it and it didn't work. Told him the same. He scheduled a replacement that very moment. Got the replacement product on the 21st since 20th was a holiday. This time the phone turned on with the display. Regained all my trust back in flipkart.
  

  Now coming to the phone, I was advised by an uncountable number of people to buy a phone with android and to avoid Nokia at all costs. Now all these hippocrates owned Nokias and only Nokias once upon a time and now simply because they didn't pair up with google, they are moving on. Bullshit! I still feel that Nokia is the king when it comes to mobile phones! Let's start off with the pros -
  

  1. Ultra premium build quality. Light Years ahead of the compeition. Still find it hard to believe that people invest the same amount of money on substandard korean plastic.
  

  2. Screen is just beautiful. PureMotion+, Clearblack, IPS and it's so smooth, it feels like you are running your hands over a block of butter. Also touch is very sensitive. Works completely fine with my leather gloves which I wear when I am riding my bike.
  

  3. Windows is an amazing OS! Sure it doesn't have the freedom and simplicity of Android but I find it to be better than Android. Purely personal opinion and I am quiet unbiased because I am upgrading from an N95 which has symbian. Also contrary to what people say, the windows market has some pretty good apps as well.
  

  4. Kickas Nokia apps. The phone comes preloaded with Nokia Maps, City Lens and Nokia Drive (Which are shown as Here Drive, Here Maps, Here City Lens post the amber update), Here Drive and Here Maps convert the phone into a highly accurate GPS device. The best part is that you can download maps and use them without having any access to network or internet. Again a boon for people like me who are frequently doing trips on motorcycles.
  

  5. Camera is Godlike! Carl Zeiss Lens, Pure View need I say more? Nokia Smart Shoot and Pro Cam (Downloadable after the amber update) just make things even better. Also 8.7 megapixels is the perfect resolution. There's no point in cramming more megapixels into such small sensors. It's just going to ruin the photo quality.
  

  6. Sound is loud and crystal clear. The only phone I found that has a better sound system is the One X+.
  

  Cons-
  

  1. It is heavy! At 189 grams it is definitely on the higher side. You can feel the bulk in your pockets.
  

  2. Battery Life is purely mediocre. I have been getting 20 hours max with medium usage. Should last a day and a half on standby.
  

  3. Phone does tend to heat up. Playing games, talking for more than 10 minutes or doing anything when the phone is on charging sure gets the mercury rising.
  

  All in all I am super satisfied with my purchase. The best part is that I got this amazing piece of Finnish technology at a mouth watering price of 18.5k. Thanks to the Diwali Sale and the 15% off on SCB cards. Although I am quiet surprised to see that so many people are having qualms with Flipkart over the returns and the replacements. Not sure if they are bluffing but my experience with WS Retail has only been good so far. Even purchased a laptop through them 6 months ago and it is running totally fine as well. Kudos to Flipkart. You have revolutionised the way Indians feel about E-commerce :)

I have never been that kind of a guy, but I never liked to leave a chance to impress a girl I meet. And my new phone, the Nokia Lumia 920, is my partner in crime when it comes to fulfilling that aspiration. With its HERE City Lens, HERE Maps, HERE Drive and HERE Transit function, I can easily get all the nearby information of the city be it eateries, discos, movie theatres and social clubs. I love to see that super-awed look on her face that follows!

The dual LED flash makes any night light up like day and imparts an undeniable vibrancy to my pics. The PureMotion HD+ 4.5-inch touchscreen display is the brightest and fastest I've ever seen. Just a feathery touch of the display and it responds in an instant. Covered with Corning Gorilla Glass 2, this display can take any kind of rough use and still look good as new. The unibody polycarbonate design is not only chic, but also makes my Lumia 920 extremely durable.
  

  Its wireless charging pad makes charging a cinch. All I have to do is place my phone on the pad and it soaks up power like a sponge soaking up on soapy water. Bought it on 1st March from Flipkart.
  
  5 Stars to Flipkart for exceptionally timely delivery.
  

  I have a Moto G and wanted a feature phone for travel/backup purposes. I previously owned a Nokia 112 and i was expecting a better version of that with Nokia 215. This phone fails at that, miserably.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Screen size is pretty great for a basic phone.
  
  2. Screen brightness at full intensity is really good and very much usable in direct sunlight.
  
  3. Aesthetically pleasing.
  
  4. Speakers are loud enough, considering the price range.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. Call quality is surprisingly mediocre. You'd expect a feature phone to get at least that right.
  
  2. Battery life is poor and nowhere near as advertised. Especially with two sim cards and some light Facebooking/Messengering/Browsing thrown in there is a good chance the battery will not even last two full days.
  
  3. Facebook app is painfully slow. I had the same app in Nokia 112 (2012) and the app has seen zero improvements since then.
  
  4. For some weird reason it has a global ringing and vibration setting that override the profiles option.
  
  5. No option/settings for system update/upgrade anywhere on the phone. Just because it is a feature phone does not mean it does not need software updates.
  
  6. There are realistically no app in the appstore, not even UC browser which was lifesaver for me on Nokia 112. Heck, Nokia 112 had an email client (which actually worked with gmail and ows), and after a system upgrade, even a working youtube player (on a 1.8 in screen :) ).
  

  Realistically, this phone is worse than Nokia's own products from 2/3 years ago.
  
  It would be decent buy for half the price (or less) that it is being sold at, not one bit more.

One of my friends recently asked me for the feedback about this phone as i am using it from 2 years, i told him my opinion and also i thought it would help others if i write review here.
  

  Buy this phone if you have below requirement.
  

  1. A decent phone for making outgoing calls and receiving incoming calls.
  

  2. A phone with USB type charger. (You can use this charger for your existing smartphone :-). This is the main reason i had shortlisted this phone. Older nokia versions has round-pin charger: -x ).
  

  3. A phone which has camera option.(Though you might not be looking for this feature, camera always comes handy in emergency situation.)
  

  4. A phone which works even after dropping it many time (You can keep dropping this phone and still expect it to work properly. My 1 year old (sorry young) niece keeps dropping (actually throws) this phone always; I just have to pick up the detached battery, back-panel, display-panel and assemble it and switch On the phone, it continues to work happily :-) )
  

  5. FM radio .
  

  6. Phone which never hangs.
  

  7. Dual-SIM.
  

  The only issue I have faced with this phone is when I receive too many messages.
  
  You can approximately save 100 messages (my observation). If you receive any message after this the phone notifies that memory is full and you would have to delete few existing messages. You can still ignore this and continue using the phone if you are least bothered about messages. :D
  

  And I dont know why this phone has 32 GB expandable memory!! But still its an added feature.

column6: Nice product from Nokia under Rs 3000
column7:
===Nokia 220===
  
  If you want a mobile phone to use just for call receiving purpose you can have this phone.
  
  I'm using Lenovo A6000 as my primary phone, and Nokia 220 as my secondary one.
  

  Hardware Specification:
  
  ------------------------

I bought this phone for my mother, and have used it for about a week. Here's my review:
  

  The specifications are available on the website already, and I will not go into details.
  
  Here are the things I felt:
  

  a) The camera (2MP) is excellent! Even if you transfer the photos to your PC, the level of detail is very good, considering the price of the phone and the fact that it is only a 2MP camera
  

  b) The phone has 3.5mm audio jack and micro USB port - great features for a phone in this price range.
  

  c) It is not easy to understand how the phone actually looks from the Flipkart images. I can tell you that the design is excellent and the phone actually looks much better than the pictures suggest. The technique for opening the back cover is novel, and I hope more phones implement this!
  

  d) The 2G internet browsing experience on this device is excellent; it also has preinstalled twitter and facebook apps
  

  e) The sound on this phone is also excellent and loud.
  

  f) This phone has a 512 MB internal memory, which is UNHEARD OF in feature phones, expecially at this price. But a slight con is that if you dont have a memory card inserted, you cannot assign images to your contacts.
  

  Overall rating: 5/5. Strongly recommend as a basic feature phone!

  I got this device 2 days after ordering it. Great delivery from Flipkart as usual, with great packaging and all.
  

  Now, after using it for 2 days, I thought I'll review this. In this age of smartphones, everyone runs after a smartphones. The main thing we're lacking with Android phones, especially is a battery. I was previously on HTC Desire 210 and then switched on HP's Voice Tab 7 for higher end needs. Apart from that, I needed a device with a good battery backup and after using Nokia's old model 2690 (S40) for 4 years, I decided to go on for a Nokia feature phone. I chose this model and I must say, I'm pretty satisfied with it.

  1. Great display. Nokia glance and the new Microsoft Windows look gives a great feeling as compared to the Symbian Models. 240x320's a decent resolution and gives a clear look.
  

  2. Great Standby. The device had like 20% charge and after fiddling around on the same battery backup for around 18 only, my battery got drained. Imagine the same on an Android device. Not possible, is it?

This device comes pre-loaded with the messenger and saves the time of turning on your smartphone or PC for browsing FB. Just gets the job done. column6: 6 reasons you might not want to buy this
column7:
I bought this phone from my nearby Nokia official reseller a few days back. The price is about the same. Writing this review to give some clarification.
  
  Customarily, let me get the PROS out first.
  
    BEAUTIFUL. Without a doubt, looks beautifully slim and very handy.
  
    LARGE SCREEN. Compared to previous iterations, screen is larger. Colours are vivid and visibility is decent. GLANCE screen works decently.
  
    THREADED MESSAGING. Like in android and windows.
  
    BACKUP. Can create backup in sd card itself.
  
    Memory card. Rarely hangs my 16gb card.
  
  Extras like voice recording, call barring, 2g Internet are present.
  

  With that, let me put why some of you may not like it.
  

    AWKWARD UI. I have used many iterations of Nokia including the N series, E series, phones like c5, xpress 5130, ASHA, 206, and lumias 720, 630 and 830. But this phone has the most awkward UI till date. Examples?
  
  1. There is no go to option on home screen. No customisable option either.
  
  2. Buttons are confusing. In alarms, you select alarm with the centre button but select the time/ringtone/other options with the left top button. Some places left top button works for saving and other places it's the centre button.
  
  In messaging, pushing the up button scrolls the thread but also works for replying. After a few hours you are not really sure which button is used for what. The old setup was more comfortable. You will get used to but it remains somewhat annoying.
  
  3. Contact search does not work from home screen i.e. typing 24 does not bring up contacts with 24 in phone no. or "ag" in name.
  
  4. The large screen looks like a waste when many features (calculator, video, music) have small controls and text, and leave most of the screen blank.
  
  5. Video player cannot even run most MP4 files. Photos cannot open png and even some jpeg files. I don't want a good display or anything, just opening a few photos/vids is enough. If you're advertising it, at least make it work. Or don't put it there in the first place. If it was a 1k phone I could accept that but a 3k phone, nope.
  

   LEGIBILITY. One of the most annoying quirks is the FONT SIZE. THE READING VIEW IN MESSAGES HAS PAINFULLY SMALL FONT SIZE. There is no way to change this. Even if you increase the font size all you can see is a bigger menu display. You can see larger text when writing but not when reading. The calendar display remains small. So does the music and many other things. Simply speaking, changing font size does not work everywhere.
  

   NUMBERPAD. Contrary to its slick look the keypad is not really tactile. Typing the third row of numbers (7,8,9) is particularly difficult in singlehanded use. The directional buttons are slightly difficult to use. There is no separate power button so if your phone gets stuck loading something, it's stuck. (As mine sometimes does.)
  

   WHATSAPP. No I am not talking about fully featured one but a basic Java version is available on opera store for most earlier phones (my mother's 206 still has it). Guess what? No opera store here. Even if you open the store in opera browser for whatsapp, you will get a "your phone is not supported" message. All you get is a Gameloft App Store that has no apps! No, I don't want fancy android apps at all! Just a basic, minimal Whatsapp support will do. It is there in older phones it sure as hell can be here.
  

   CALL CLARITY. Again, falls short of previous (basic) phones by a distinct margin. I have to keep speaker volume max and even then, it's not as good.
  

   INBUILT STORE. You get a Gameloft store which lets you buy simple games for over 50 bucks. No apps. None. Just don't give me that store at all please. I don't need it. Nobody does. The opera store is better but not supported.
  

   There are other small quirks which may be ignored. You can't switch off keypad backlight. The "Files" app does not support selecting/moving/sharing multiple files. (Go to photos/videos to share multiple photos/vids. Anything else you can't.) No playlists supported in music player. Call recording is absent.
  

  CONCLUSION. I would still say that 225 isn't such a bad phone. But it's a misfit. If all you want is a basic phone for calls/messaging/torch then you're better off buying 105/108/130 etc. On the other hand if you want a feature phone, I think Samsung metro works better. But if you want a beautiful phone then this is your pick. Definitely not recommended for the elderly!

column6: It is not OLD Nokia Anymore. Don't be decieved by Looks
column7:
As a loyal customer of various Nokia handsets since the past 15 years I expected that the Nokia-225 would be a contemporary upgrade. However, i am shocked by the lack of even basic features which existed on every other low-end Nokia handset which i had used earlier 1) CONTACTS 1a) No provision to store more than one number against each contact. How does one store the mobile no., office nos., home no. and fax no. of a contact? What if the contact has more than one mobile no. or office no.? 1b) Contact names cannot exceed 14 characters. No provision to enter first name and last name separately. If two persons have a common first name (which is very common in India) and need to be distinguished with an identifier, how can their names be entered separately as two different records in the Contacts List?. Try this - (1) Ramakrishnan - Hyderabad; (2) Ramakrishnan - Bangalore; (3) Ramakrishnan (3) New Jersey 1c) No provision to add email ids of the contact. 1d) No provision to add a postal address of the contact 1e) No provision to add notes against a contact (NOTE: All the above fields against CONTACTS were provider in all the other Nokia handsets which i have used since the past 15 years, except this one!!!) 2) MESSAGING (SMS) 2a)- Messages do not get saved in standard folders named as "INBOX"/ "SENT" / "OUTBOX". The conversation format is extremely cumbersome to locate any message. 2b)- After typing a message if it is not sent immediately, it does not get saved in the "DRAFTS" folder as with other Nokia handsets. Instead, in Nokia-225 the message just disappears !!! IT IS REASONABLE FOR ANY CUSTOMER TO EXPECT THAT MORE RECENT MODELS WOULD HAVE ALL THE BASIC FEATURES OF THE OLDER MODELS BUT THIS PHONE DOESN'T HAVE EVEN THE 50% OF WHAT OLDER NOKIA MODELS HAVE.

As an example, when you press the green answer button to receive an incoming call, there is a big lag leading to a confusion whether the call has been received. And then you press the answering button again which puts the call on hold and that is issritating. The trick is to receive the call, and literally WAIT for 4-5 seconds before you can finally start speaking.

Hey Everyone,
  

  I got this device 2 days after ordering it. Great delivery from Flipkart as usual, with great packaging and all.
  

  Now, after using it for 2 days, I thought I'll review this. In this age of smartphones, everyone runs after a smartphones. The main thing we're lacking with Android phones, especially is a battery. I was previously on HTC Desire 210 and then switched on HP's Voice Tab 7 for higher end needs. Apart from that, I needed a device with a good battery backup and after using Nokia's old model 2690 (S40) for 4 years, I decided to go on for a Nokia feature phone. I chose this model and I must say, I'm pretty satisfied with it.
  

  Pros:
  

  1. Great display. Nokia glance and the new Microsoft Windows look gives a great feeling as compared to the Symbian Models. 240x320's a decent resolution and gives a clear look.
  

  2. Great Standby. The device had like 20% charge and after fiddling around on the same battery backup for around 18 only, my battery got drained. Imagine the same on an Android device. Not possible, is it?
  

  3. Internet: Most of us have that family or friends who are on Facebook or Twitter. This device comes pre-loaded with the messenger and saves the time of turning on your smartphone or PC for browsing FB. Just gets the job done. Yahoo, Twitter, Nokia Xpress and other stuff provide pretty good speed to catch up. Device supports GPRS upto 84.6KBPS and even Edge. The speed is just amazing.
  

  4. Great sound clarity and smart volume for protection organ damage (ear).
  

  5. Decent Camera.
  

  6. Decent OS and UI. Reminds me of the times I've had Lumia 520. Feels much familiar. The candybar design makes the device even better to hold.
  

  Cons:
  

  1. No Games Store
  

  2. Low Light Photography

  Overall, I must say, it's a a perfect first internet device for someone less concerned about megapixels and multi-core processors.
