I've been using this for a month now and I'm ever more convinced that Lumia 620 is undoubtedly THE BEST PHONE FOR THE PRICE POINT. Windows phone is really convenient to use and the minimalist design and in-built applications such as music and video player, MS Office and PDF reader make life easy. I've tried to break up the review into  the following sub-topics. Also since several of the previous reviews involve similar views, I'll keep it short and to the point.
  

  Design & Build - 5/5
  

  It's the best-looking phone I've ever laid my hands on. The back panel is pretty sturdy and has a premium finish, feels very nice. However I found inserting the SIM card into the tray a bit of an agony. I guess it's same with all the smartphones these days; microSIM.
  

  Operating System - 5/5
  

  Fast, fluid and dramatically beautiful, as Microsoft puts it. The Swanky Start screen is a refreshing change from the boring and ubiquitous Android App tray. You can manage all your accounts be it gmail, facebook or twitter. All in one place and you never need to login to your account. This strong social network integration is arguably the best part Windows phone 8. About the File explorer, you really don't need one on WP when you have the beautiful hubs for music, videos, and the likes.
  

  And task manager? I don't give a damn. This is Windows Phone and it's not app-centric as Android is. Lags? Extremely rare only when you overload it with 5-6 simultaneous apps. Multi-tasking? Quite convenient with the Home and Back buttons.
  

  App Store - 4/5
  

  Doesn't even come close to Android or iOS, we all know that, but the Windows Phone is getting there and fast. You get almost all essential apps that are on andriod as well. It is to mentioned that the WP store is not filled too many crappy apps that are of no use (as in Play Sore). And every app comes at much smaller size than at Play Store which means you'll never need your SD card to install apps. The in-built phone memory is of added value in this scenario; lots of space.
  

  But Nokia Music is proves to be so good. I no longer browse the web for music. Free offline music as well with mix radio. They've got all the music genres out there and with a fast data connection (or wifi) download is pretty fast. The categories of top songs and artist bio all amazing. Love it!
  

  Camera - 4.5/5
  

  As would expect from Nokia, pretty good and evidently leads the pack at the price range. Nokia adds even more value with the custom lenses like panorama (works beautifully well), smart shoot, blink, cinemagraph etc.
  

  Battery - 3.5/5
  

  A minor glitch there, only a 1300 mah cell? Nokia should have really put in a 1500 mah one, considering that Lumia 520 has a 1430 mah battery :(
  
  But with average usage, the phone lasts for well over a day. However GPRS browsing seems to quickly drain the battery by a lot. Wifi would be a better option. But I don't think most smartphones will offer a battery backup of more than a day, so there, there.
  


  I can go on forever. But on every other front you could think of, Nokia Lumia strikes the right notes. I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who's looking at a phone at this price range. I'm not arguing that WP is better than Android or iOS. It's just that at the mid-range market Windows Phone devices offer much better than Andriod devices which struggle to give you a smooth user experience as the flagship (30-40k devices). With WP, the performance is uniform across all devices. Come flagship devices I'd be wise to stick to Android devices (Samsung, HTC). Windows Phone is still growing as an OS and it begs to differ from the mainstream operating systems out there.
  

  Kudos to Nokia and Microsoft for giving us phenominal bang for the buck.

column6: High return rates and WP8 needs a lot of improvement
column7:
First, WP8 is nowhere close to iOS or Android. The tile UI is cool but that's about the only positive thing you can say about WP8. There're a couple of cool apps from Nokia (Drive and Music) but they don't compensate for the lack of apps for a lot of other things a smartphone's supposed to do. Let me list out the bad stuff -
  

  1) You absolutely need to connect your phone to a PC to manage your music.
  
  2) There's no file manager app. You cannot manage storage on your SD card without connecting to a PC.
  
  3) You can upload pics and videos, docs and app lists directly to Skydrive (you get 7 GB of free cloud storage) but there's no option to upload music. That would be very useful to use with Nokia's unlimited music subscription for 6 months. You download whatever you want and archive it in the cloud.
  
  4) The facebook app by MS sucks. I don't see notifications for messages or friend requests. Other facebook apps are equally bad.
  
  5) There's no quora app (yet).
  
  6) Contact sync with gmail doesn't work. I can only see empty profiles of gmail contacts (no phone numbers or email ids).
  
  7) No temple run. No instagram.
  
  8) Frequent crashes.
  

  Further, this phone suffers from higher than normal return rates.
  

  I myself received a defective piece. It worked for a week but with battery problems. Battery would drain out extremely quickly - 100% to 25% in a couple of hours. Suddenly, yesterday the phone wouldn't turn on. I tried charging it for half-hour but it still wouldn't turn on. I called Flipkart about this and also told them about how it could be a faulty battery.
  

  They asked me to confirm this from a Nokia Care center and get a DOA to get a replacement. I've been to three Nokia cares and Priority centers and nobody would give me a DOA certificate. When I informed Flipkart about this, they told me they escalated the issue to some higher department and I should expect to receive a call from them in a day. Called them today and they ask me to wait another 24 hrs.
  

  The sad thing is this was supposed to be a gift to my Mom. I really hope flipkart resolves this somehow.

column6: Paltry Phone..!! Not good at all..!!
column7:
The phone is good from look,design and make perspective considering the price range and also offers an ok ok camera, however that is the only thing likeable about it for the price you pay for it. The phone fails fails miserably with its dialler fucntionality. The phone is not instantly responsive while making or receiving calls and makes you feel as though you have bought a phone from the early 1950's... There is a considerable delay in the phone recongnising the user action thus leaving the user perplexed whether they performed that action. As an example, when you press the green answer button to receive an incoming call, there is a big lag leading to a confusion whether the call has been received. And then you press the answering button again which puts the call on hold and that is issritating. The trick is to receive the call, and literally WAIT for 4-5 seconds before you can finally start speaking.
  
  Except whilst dialling a number where the phone recognises the numbers you dialled instantly,lagging will be experienced while reading/typing messages, looking up for contacts, adding new contacts in your phone or while performing any other such action.
  

  Hence, i recommend that it is not a good phone to buy..!! Recommended- refrain from buying/putting your hard earned 2.5k over it... You will surely end up not loving it.!!

Hey Everyone,
  

  I got this device 2 days after ordering it. Great delivery from Flipkart as usual, with great packaging and all.
  

  Now, after using it for 2 days, I thought I'll review this. In this age of smartphones, everyone runs after a smartphones. The main thing we're lacking with Android phones, especially is a battery. I was previously on HTC Desire 210 and then switched on HP's Voice Tab 7 for higher end needs. Apart from that, I needed a device with a good battery backup and after using Nokia's old model 2690 (S40) for 4 years, I decided to go on for a Nokia feature phone. I chose this model and I must say, I'm pretty satisfied with it.
  

  Pros:
  

  1. Great display. Nokia glance and the new Microsoft Windows look gives a great feeling as compared to the Symbian Models. 240x320's a decent resolution and gives a clear look.
  

  2. Great Standby. The device had like 20% charge and after fiddling around on the same battery backup for around 18 only, my battery got drained. Imagine the same on an Android device. Not possible, is it?
  

  3. Internet: Most of us have that family or friends who are on Facebook or Twitter. This device comes pre-loaded with the messenger and saves the time of turning on your smartphone or PC for browsing FB. Just gets the job done. Yahoo, Twitter, Nokia Xpress and other stuff provide pretty good speed to catch up. Device supports GPRS upto 84.6KBPS and even Edge. The speed is just amazing.
  

  4. Great sound clarity and smart volume for protection organ damage (ear).
  

  5. Decent Camera.
  

  6. Decent OS and UI. Reminds me of the times I've had Lumia 520. Feels much familiar. The candybar design makes the device even better to hold.
  

  Cons:
  

  1. No Games Store
  

  2. Low Light Photography
  

  3. Light Body
  

  Overall, I must say, it's a a perfect first internet device for someone less concerned about megapixels and multi-core processors.

Along with the Nokia Camera there are other photography apps as well such as the Creative Studio, Bing Vision, Cinemagraph, Storyteller etc. I am glad that it has been provided with a Quad Core processor which is why all the apps functions so smoothly and with a great speed. Moreover my Nokia Lumia 630 DS facilitates typing at a blazing fast speed. Only by swiping on the screen I can type on and this makes the entire mechanism faster. column6: Really great phone for the amount.
column7:
Edit on 20/06/2015.
  
  Now after an year of usage, I can vouch the durability of this phone. I have only used this in "Single SIM" mode and I am totally satisfied. I have just ordered Lenovo A6000+, reason being, my office only allows configuring office mail on either Android or iOS and I cannot afford an Apple phone now. I am handing this over to my wife, she was reluctant at the start and now she wanted it.
  

  After a year, I can re-iterate - phone is too good for the price or even a class up.
  
  ================================================================
  
  I am writing this review after an extended usage of more than 6 months.
  
  Initially when I bought this phone, I migrated from Android, I was feeling bit let down and was finding it hard to come to terms with my purchase. The "lack of user friendliness", "lack of applications in store" etc. were really pinching me. It took me about a month's time to get used to Windows eco-system. But, once I was used to it, I love it. Believe me, I am still "learning" it.
  

  I use my phone primarily for "phone" purpose and then my wife uses it for gaming. I actually bought it as a gift to my wife, however, she was reluctant to use it at the beginning and I "owned" it. Now she wants it badly. Other than "phone", WhatsApp, mail, "NEWS" application by Bing is heavily used. I have only used it in "single sim" mode.
  
  Phone function:- This is what I use this phone mostly. Network catches pretty quickly and really hugs to the last available piece of it as well. In-call voice is loud and clear, other party can hear me clearly (even when I am outdoor in noisy environment) as well (in fact, this is better than how I hear), during the conf calls, I use the loudspeaker and it is loud and clear as well. On an average, in a day, I will be on calls between 2-3 hours (and when I do work from home, it will be for 4-5 hours) and if my day is bad, it could even extend to 8-9 hours and the phone never panics. The ear-phone getting hot is not much experienced by me as I use loud speaker to a great extend or else a bluetooth head set.
  

  Gaming:- I play Asphalt 8 and my wife plays candycrush. Asphalt 8 is a graphically challenging game for a phone which just has 512MB RAM, but this phone handles it quite nicely without any lag. And more importantly, this will not become an hot iron box even after playing Asphalt 8, for, say, about an hour or so.
  

  Battery:- I am always on network either mobile net or Wifi and am on call for atleast 3 hours in a day. Still, the battery stays for atleast a day. If I play in the night after this heavy usage, I will have to charge it over night. I normally do not charge overnight, but, when I am awake and remove the charger as an when it reaches 100%. "Battery Saver" kicks in properly and preserves whatever little battery you have and you can customise this.
  

  App store/ Lumia exclusive apps:- I should say, we may not find here all application which is there in Android store, however, you will get a lot of related apps and at times, you find better ones. I never had faced an issue where I was stranded due to non-availability of a particular app/ it's alternative.
  

  Sunlight legibility:- There is no ambient light sensor, rather you have 3 options "Low/ Medium/ High" and you can decide how low the low setting should go or how high the high setting should go etc. it is fully customisable. So you will not face issue viewing in bright sun, however, you will have to manually toggle the settings. Good thing, if you have a password locked screen, you need not unlock the screen to toggle the brightness settings, you can just swipe down, then tap the option to change the settings.
  

  Camera:- it is a 5 MP rear camera without flash. However, the images are too good for this. It can definitely be compared with some of the 8MP shooters out there in the market.
  

  Cons - Coming to the shortcomings (according to me)
  
  There is no front facing camera, but I bought this knowing this shortcoming.
  
  The battery could have been better which might make it a true "charge once in 24 hours" piece.
  
  Multi tasking is the Apple iOS way, if you move away from the app, the app stops and kicks in again when you access the app again. (this I felt when I opened a webpage and moved to another app while the page was still loading, when I came back, it started from the point where I left). This should have been a true multi tasking phone, but however, this limitation will be overcome in Windows 10 (if I read the reviews correctly).
  
  Do I recommend this to others? yes, a big YES. If you have only this much money, yes this is right piece for you.
  

  Most beautiful feature - Windows 10 when released will be available to my phone as well.

The absence of a front facing camera and a led flash led me to think about giving it 4 out of 5 stars but its other overwhelming features made me change my mind.
  

  1. Camera : Do not judge the quality of a camera by the pixel count. This camera is one of the best camera in the 5-megapixel category, noise levels are noticeably low, the sensor is a brilliant one, the level of details is amazing considering price. Use the apps pro shot and 4blend hdr for best results.
  

  2. Music : The absence of an equalizer does not make it a worthless device. music quality is superb, it is very precisely optimized and one would not feel the need for an equalizer moreover an equalizer distorts sound output if not optimized in the pro-manner. But do not judge it's quality by using low quality headphones, the impedance and frequency range are important factors in determining audio output.
  

  3. Sensors : It lacks ambient light sensor and a proximity sensor. the lack of an ambient light sensor is replaced by Nokia's top-notch polarizing filter known as the clear black display. the lack of a proximity sensor is replaced by the procedure of automatic screen lock when the screen comes in contact with the face or the ear. This device includes Nokia's newest technology called sensor-core, in which motion data is gathered by the health apps without wasting battery charge.
  

  4. Display : Not a 720p display, but the presence of the clear black display gives it a vehement punch, the colours appear more crispier, the contrast levels are excellent, blacks are more black and whites are more white.
  

  5. Performance : You may need to forget about the term 'lags'. There is no visible lag. Wp 8.1 is optimized in the most pristine manner. basemark os II benchmark results will be in and around 440 to 450 which clearly is more than many upper range devices. The lack of 1 gigs of ram will not hurt much mainly because of the Snapdragon quadcore, and it is seen that 512mb variants of 1gb ram games are flooding the store. The apps in the store WILL suffice.
  

  Advice : After buying the device try not to use it heavily for 4-5 days, the phone optimizes itself for impeccable performance, use it after some days and you will get to know what you behold. Do use the wi-fi with the battery saver turned on, it would result in low downloading speeds.
  

  Feature : A good feature is the battery saver. While turned on it under clocks the processor cores to save battery life and it does a fantastic job.
  

  If you want to watch full screen videos and you feel that the on screen buttons are a hindrance then download the app 'files' and play the desired video from the folder itself, that way the on screen buttons will be disabled during playback.

column6: Nokia Lumia 630 DS: Dual Sim Smartphone Within Budget
column7:
I love the colourful and the bright factor of my Nokia Lumia 630 DS. It came in different colours and has a matte finish which is why despite it's popping colours it doesn't end up looking too flashy. And the good news for me is that I can change the cover of my phone as I wish and sport the colour of my choice. The colourful and customizable Live Tiles looks wonderful on the 11.43 cm screen. The IPS LCD and the Clear Black technology combine to make a spectacular display possible on my phone. Anything from mere texts to videos exhibit themselves at their best. Also it has several useful and top apps pre loaded on it. Whatsapp, WeChat, Line, Linkedin etc are few of the preloaded apps on my phone. There is also a huge collection of free apps on the Windows Phone store from where I can download any app I wish to. The size and the number of the apps I download are never a thing to worry about as there is ample space for these apps and files. It's 8 GB internal storage itself is huge and it can also be further extended upto 128 GB which is a great relief to me. I get all the updates from my social networking accounts, my chats and settings etc at the Action centre. But the most amazing feature on my Nokia Lumia 630 DS is the Word Flow keypad. I can type really fast on it. It is just the swiping mechanism that helps me type sentences with a blazing fast speed. It is otherwise a fast phone and it is due to the Quad Core processor because of which all the apps run smoothly. 1830 mAh capacitated battery ensures a great battery life for the Nokia Lumia 630 DS. It seems to hardly drain out even if I am using it all day long. The Dual Sim is ofcourse an added benefit as it makes a lot of things easier for me like call management or reducing call costs or data costs by adopting the best available plans.

I got bored after using my galaxy s3 for 2 years. Since I bought it for 38k, I could not switch phone even if I wanted. Thanks to the rain in Delhi, finally my s3 got damaged. But this time I knew what I had to buy. A simple and different phone which does the job nicely. These are some pros and cons of LUMIA 630.
  

  Pros (Hardware):
  
  1. Good looking
  

  2. lightweight
  

  3. clear screen
  

  4. 4.5 inch screen size seems idle for the hand.
  

  5. good sound
  

  6. nice battery backup.

  Cons (Hardware):
  
  1. Screen is not HD. After switching from a HD screen I could feel the pixelation on this non-HD screen. Hence I have reduced reading articles on the phone.
  

  2. Camera is average. Just does the job. Nothing great about it.
  

  3. No light sensor. no auto brightness feature.
  

  4. No proximity sensor. It uses some other technology to detect that your phone is near your ear. But if you are sweating while talking, then this technology fails and you might not get the screen for a while unless you wipe the sweat on the phone.
  

  5. Low RAM for gaming. Some high definition games like AE moto GP were lagging. Other small games run fine though.
  

  Pros(Software):
  
  1. Windows is great and the apps are just awesome.
  

  2. No lag whatsoever.
  

  3. Wonderful live tiles with live backgrounds.
  

  5. Customizable themes.
  

  6. There are some pre-installed bing apps like travel, health, news which are very good.
  

  7. Whatsapp, facebook, twitter, instagram apps are very nice.
  

  8. Nokia Mix Radio. Say bye bye to songs.pk and song transfers.
  

  9. 15 GB onedrive cloud space.
  

  Cons(Software):
  
  1. No Cortana in India yet. News says it wont be available in India by this year at least. :-(
  

  2. No Google apps except one basic Google search app. Say bye bye to hangouts.
  


  Well that's all. Just think about your usage and what you want from a phone which costs 9000-10000 rs. If you see value for money, go for it.

  After spending a decent amount of time with the Asha 502, testing its battery life, camera, Internet connectivity, gaming capabilities and much more, here is what we think about this budget handset.
  
  Build quality and design
  
  The Nokia Asha 502 is extremely comfortable to hold, as its sharp corners give the user a better grip and reduce the chances of it slipping and falling.The entire back panel and all four edges of Asha 502 are encased in a transparent material, giving the handset a crystallized effect.
  
  Display
  
  The Nokia Asha 502's 3-inch screen is smaller than those of other devices in the same price segment. Users coming from phones with 4-5-inch screens might be able to get used to it, but if you like the feel of phablet devices that are currently popular, you'll find the small screen cumbersome to operate.
  

  The Nokia Asha 502's multi-touch screen features a QVGA (320 x 240 pixels) resolution. The screen can display only 256,000 colours as opposed to the full range of 1.6 million colours that is the usual standard. When set to full brightness, the screen is easily visible under direct sunlight.
  
  Software/Interface
  
  The Nokia Asha 502 runs on the latest Asha OS, version 1.1, which is an update to the software used by the Asha 501. The OS uses simple swipe gestures for most actions, and the back button is mainly used to close apps and return to the main menu screen.
  
  Camera
  
  Even though it's a budget device, the Asha 502 has a 5-megapixel fixed-focus rear camera with a f/2.4 aperture and an LED flash with a range of one metre. There's no front-facing camera and very few camera software features.
  

  The camera interface of Asha 502 is pretty easy to operate. The camera app can be directly accessed from the lock screen by swiping upwards. Once open, you can long-press on the screen to access the camera settings which include flash adjustment options, self-timer, white balance, filters, camera shutter sound and a choice of five resolutions.

column6: The perfect QWERTY phone for casual usage
column7:
I ordered this for my wife skeptically. Because, many reviewers felt it is slow. But, after I got the phone, I realized that it is the WiFi streaming on YouTube which is slow, and not the phone itself.
  

  PROS
  
  -Large, readable display
  
  -Comfortable to hold, and not too large
  
  -Dual SIM (Full size)
  
  -Smooth navigation and works flawlessly
  
  -Good battery backup. 2 days on moderate usage.
  
  -Build Quality is good
  
  -Excellent call quality. No drops, no echos.
  
  -WiFi, good if you have a wireless BB at home or workplace (for FB / whatsapp) saves some operator data charges.
  

  CONS
  
  -Buttons are little small, people with big thumbs must use the nails. Tactile feedback is little on the harder side.
  
  -S40 OS which doesnt offer many apps
  
  -Camera is just okay. 2MP photos, and 174x144 Video.
  
  -YouTube streaming via WiFi is slow. Probably it is the app, and not the phone.
  

  Overall, this phone is good for people who makes a lot of calls, texts often, updates FB / whatsapp. Do not expect smartphone performance, as this is not a smartphone, but a upper-entry-level Dual SIM phone with QWERTY keypad. It may lack some features of Android (in the same price range), but the build quality and robust performance of Asha 210 compensates the rest.

column7:
I have been using this phone for nearly 20 days now, and after reading some of the blatantly biased reviews, have decided to write one myself. I shall only provide reasons as to why it is a good investment, and why not.
  

  BUY IF:
  
  1. You want a large, reasonably sharp screen.
  
  2. Lag drives you crazy. (WP7 is light years ahead of Android in this department).
  
  3. You thrive on social media. (Deep integration of Facebook, only iOS 6 matches it).
  
  4. You want excellent build quality (it is a Nokia, after all) and looks.
  
  5. You want a visually pleasing and user-friendly OS.
  
  6. You want MS Office for free (don't think an average user needs it, though).
  

  AVOID IF:
  
  1. You are an app junkie. (WP has significantly less apps than Android or iOS).
  
  2. You want a portable media center. (though 2.8 GB of media should be enough for normal people)
  
  3. You don't own/frequently access a PC/Laptop. (All data is synced using Zune only).
  
  4. Gaming enthusiast. (The processor/RAM can't handle most existing games).
  
  5. Are anything more than a casual photographer (No LED flash, or 720p recording).
  

  Hope this helps :)

column6: why you should not buy windows phone
column7:
Before I tell you why I don't recommend Windows Phone, I must tell you that I have been using lumia 520 for last 45 days. Phone is quite good in all aspects be it Call Quality, be it UI . Display is super good and touchscreen is awesome. People keep on complaining about apps, but trust me we have all the useful apps in Windows Phone which we need for daily use. Some are even better than Android. So these are the best parts of my review. By this time I am sure, you must have read the Review title atleast 2 times that why I don't recommend windows phone.
  
  So here it goes.  lumia has 7.1 GB internal memory in which we can install apps. Mind that, we can install apps only in internal memory not on SD card. out of 7.1 GB, 4 GB is user accessible which is quite enough for installing apps. Assuming that an average app takes up 20 MB of space, we can install 200 apps. Even the most addicted phone users dont need that many apps , so memory is not a problem. But wait. when we see the breakup of the memory, it is divided into 4 sections.
  
  1.Apps
  
  2.System
  
  3. Music ,Photos and all
  
  4. Others.
  

  The fourth section 'Others' is inaccessible by users and we cant delete anything in that. When you purchase a new phone , the size is around 50 MB. But as you keep on using it , its size will grow bigger and bigger. It is like the %temp% folder in our computer which keeps some random data. and is of no use to us. I will give an example how this memory gets consumed.
  
  Assume you have 500 MB of memory left in your phone. You install an app of 30 MB. Remaining is 470 MB. But you will get only 465 MB. This extra 5 MB got consumed in Other section. Now you  uninstall the app. You should get 495 MB. But you will get only 490 MB. So, there is effectively no change in the contents of phone because you installed and uninstalled an app and net is zero.  But what we lost is 10 MB without any reason. This kind of memory consumption will happen every time whatever you do in your phone. SO , right now in my phone , the 'Other' section is consuming as much as 2.6 gb of space without any reason. and you can not delete it. Now if I watch any youtube video or anything which requires phone space, it says that your phone memory is low. And this consumption will keep on increasing. I checked Windows forum and hundreds of people are facing this problem. I will have to reset the phone if I want to delete that Others section. You will lose all data in your phone if you do that.
  
  So guys, initial experience is going to be awesome with windows phone , but trust me , after 50 -60 days , you will find yourself in the same situation as I am in right now.
  
  Rest is your choice.

Your videos, photos, music, and radio- all in the same place. Connect the phone to your computer, put in some music in a matter of seconds and your good to go. Music lovers will end up loving it but the ones who want high end graphics for gaming and stuff should  also consider this. Doesn't exactly give you the high end you expected, but does the job. One touch photo uploads and auto fix make you feel less of a need for a flash. I would say, this is an optimum phone for someone who takes the occasional snap and, well, is a social person.

column6: Surprisingly good phone at a throwaway price....
column7:
I was a loyal customer of Nokia up until 3 yrs ago. My first Nokia phone was 6300, then 3600 slide and finally N73 Music Edition. But, after buying that crappy N73 phone I was miserable. I think I used most of my awakened state running from one Nokia Care to another. It had so many problems that I finally got rid of the phone (Wasn't easy to find a buyer) and switched to Blackberry. I lost my faith in Nokia completely. But, after using this little piece of hardware I think I've regained some of that faith again.
  
  The phone looks pretty basic by it's looks. I mean it doesn't even have an usb port despite having decent expandable memory capacity. But, if you dig deeper then you'll realize that you can't ask for a better phone at this price range.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. It uses Symbian S40 platform which in  my opinion is the best bug free platform there is. Of course its not as fancy as Android or Windows but it gets the job done.
  
  2. It is java enabled. you can download java applications such as offline dictionary, notepad, games from getjar.com. Or, you can just look for files with .jar extension.
  
  3. Music quality is pretty decent both in loudspeaker and headset.
  
  4. Camera is VGA quality but not obscure. I once took a picture of a diagram and could understand (with a little bit of struggle) it properly.
  
  5. Internet speed is not bad for 2g. I downloaded 2 music files, 1st was 5.5 mb and the 2nd was 7.4 mb. both got downloaded in around 10-15 minutes (Aircel).
  
  6. It supports nokia themes/ .nth files. you can make your own themes using nokia theme studio.
  
  7. Battery is unexpectedly good. I've listened to music for around 1-1.5 hr since yesterday, accessed my twitter, surfed around wikipedia and spoken to my friends for like 2 hrs yet I've lost only 1 bar of battery charge up until now.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. 1 con i found so far is that when I apply any custom themes (other than those came with the handset) the phone remains on even after I switch it off. So every time I have to switch it off twice.
  

  So, If you are looking for a decent phone at this price range, then I'll definitely recommend this one.

  1) VERY long battery life - the main reason why I bought this phone. It easily lasts 2 weeks on a single charge with an average of 1 hour talking everyday. I am using this handset with a single SIM to maximize battery life.
  

  2) The keypad is soft but there is tactile feedback which makes typing text quite comfortable.
  

  3) Charges pretty fast for such a large battery. Around 2 hrs is all it takes.
  

  4) Call quality is superb. No problems in voice clarity or echo which is present in some other low end Nokia handsets.
  

  5) At just 86g, this handset is as light as it gets.
  


  Cons:
  
  1) Disappointed with the quality of the bundled earpiece. I know I cant expect much at this price but the included earpiece is just not adequate for listening any kind of music. Just use to it for voice calls and expect nothing more.
  

  2) The MicroSD slot is behind the battery and is hard to reach. This is a major con since there is no data connectivity port on the phone either. So you must take out the MicroSD the hard way and use a card reader everytime you want to load something onto the card.
  

  3) Max ringtone volume could have been louder as its not audible sometimes on the road.
  


  Conclusion:
  
  On the whole I think its an excellent basic phone for anyone who just wants to make calls and text away. It will also complement your smartphone well. The battery life is a huge plus point, which makes this a great emergency phone.

It is one of the factors why so many people are having pain in their ears after talking for long. The Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is the amount of radiation that is absorbed by your phone while talking. So, the greater the radiation that your phone absorbs, the greater is the damage cause to your ears. For eg. In terms of safety, 1.5W/kg is more dangerous than 1W/kg which is more harmful than 0.8 W/Kg and so on.
  

  4. Windows 8 did not have the option of manually killing tasks until now. But with General Release 3, which is expected to be out for the public soon, it addresses this problem and many others, in addition to introducing some new features of its own. This will make the phone's interface even more beautiful than it already is.
  

  As for the people saying that there are no apps in the Windows phone market, there are already 1,20,000 Certified apps at the time of writing this review. column6: I bought this phone and has been using it for a week now. Read on:
column7:
Absolutely unusable in bed, the corners prick my had when I try to type, and Windows Phone 8 doesn't let me turn off screen rotation which is a pain (hope this comes in a further update)!
  

  The phone is built rock solid and feels very premium, my brother has a SGS3 and comparatively my 920 is much better.
  

  The brightness can be adjusted to only three levels, low, medium and high. With low still being pretty bright. Auto Brightness works like a charm and brings brightness to a much lower level than the default "low" setting, but I wish I could have done that manually so as to conserve my battery.
  

  Battery lasts a day if used judiciously. It was very average for the first two days, which disappointed me, but it improved drastically after a couple of full charges and discharges! :O
  

  Nokia Music, Nokia Maps and Nokia City Lens. Damn!! Love these. And also the fact that I get a free subscription to Nokia Music for an year (legal, hq music) gets me every time. It even has Malayalam and Tamil music apart from Hindi and World.
  

  I can download attachments from email but I do not know where it gets stored, which means that I cannot delete them manually. They get deleted automatically as and when the email gets deleted from my inbox (sync settings allow you to sync email from the past 3 days, past 7 days, past 2 weeks and any time).
  

  There isn't a file manager which lets me browse through the files on my phone. You cannot find one on the Windows Marketplace either.
  

  But of course, you can drag and drop files to and from your pc which makes transferring songs and videos between my phone and pc very easy.
  

  Windows Phone 8 is fluidic, does not crash or hang and is extremely user friendly (might take you a day or two or even three to get used to it though). The Facebook, Twitter and Email integration works like a charm. It is much cleaner and exciting than Android, though not as customisable.
  

  Coming from a Samsung Galaxy SII running Jellybean, these are the things I liked and disliked about the Lumia 920.
  

  Overall I am satisfied with the 920, and does not regret my decision to buy a windows phone.

Nokia being on its last legs has decided to go all out on their Lumia series with the hope of capturing the early glories of its hey day. Guess what, it shows through on their phones, be it ergonomics, design, style or application.
  

  When you switch on the phone, the first thing that strikes you is the innovative and beautifully designed tiles that sets it apart from any of its competitors. Combine that along with the option of changing the tile colors, size and look, you've got the freedom of customizing to suit your needs. Don't get me started on the resolution. It easily is above the Iphone 5 or Samsung S3. The tiles are constantly changing and when you play a track on the phone, the music tile scrolls the name of the song and the artist. Certain apps like dictionary (free) keeps changing and the last viewed word is constantly on the tile. This helps believe in learning one word a day. Small changes like these make this a very practical phone.
  

  The phone is also extremely user friendly and offers many small but innovative changes that make the phone such a joy to use. Almost anything (contacts, videos, photos, apps, individual tracks etc) can be "pinned" to the main screen for easy access. This has made my life a lot easier and can help in quickly accessing things that I often use. The best part about this phone is its multi tasking ability. I have often opened 5 or 6 different windows (application, contacts, music, messaging) at the same time and holding the back button for a second shrinks all the windows "mac style" and the desired window can immediately be accessed without losing the current window. Even when multiple windows are opened (5 -6), the phone never slows down.
  

  The nokia app store, though not as diverse and loaded like the Apple store, still provides a lot of useful applications. Nokia Maps provides the option of downloading a map of any country and can be accessed offline. This is such a blessing when I need directions and don't have good internet connection. Nokia Music provides 1 year of unlimited subscription and can be used to download albums free of cost.
  

  As far as practicality goes, this phone is right there at the top. I have used IOS for the last 4 years and I found the transition from Apple to Nokia seamless. The contact list is alphabetically arranged and the tile can be clicked on to bring about the entire alphabet list to quickly navigate to the desired contact. While the Iphone has the closely packed side bars which quite often misses the correct input and takes me either to the preceding or the succeeding alphabet.
  

  The entire history of a contact can be accessed either through the calls list or the contact list (swiping either side will lead to the entire message thread, photo album, facebook, mail etc of the contact). Such small changes make a huge difference when using the phone. The only gripe I have with this phone is the absence of customized labels which IOS provides. you are presented only with generic contacts titles (home 1, office 1 etc) which leads to confusion especially when you have friends who use 2 or 3 phones.
  

  The camera is one of the key features of the phone and has one of the best low light performance of any phone on the market today. Being a photographer, I can confidently say that this phone is a solidwhen it comes to capturing photos with very little light and its low light performance is very well ahead of any phone. for the geeks, the camera goes upto ISO 800.
  

  There is so much to be said about this phone but I there is nothing like the joy of discovery. I am not a Nokia fanboy (the last nokia phone I had was the 7610 way back in 2006). I have been waiting for quite sometime to buy this phone since it was introduced and I am glad. The phone has exceeded my best expectations.
  

  Pro's:
  
  Excellent ergonomics
  
  Beautifully designed
  
  The screen resolution is simply amazing
  
  Hugely customizable
  
  practical
  
  Very good camera
  
  Small innovative tweaks that go a long way
  

  Cons:
  
  No customizable contact label
  
  32gb with no external memory slot
  
  Slightly big (but you'll get over it soon once you see its resolution and the quality)
  
  limited app store
  

  For those of you who are saving up for a smart phone, go ahead and buy this phone without a thought, you'll love it. Everyone (friends, family) who've seen this phone have fallen instantly in love with its alluring beauty and once I've given them a taste of what this phone can do, they are hooked. These are guys who used Iphone's and Samsung for years. Nokia is back with the same innovative mindset that helped them establish a monopoly on the mobile market in India over a decade ago.
  

  I very rarely post reviews of products I have purchased and I decided to post this because I am bit partial to Nokia (my first phone was a Nokia) and hope this review convinces someone to buy this brilliant phone that may otherwise be buried under the over saturated, big brand name market of the smart phone

  5) No file manager makes life really difficult, like really really.
  

  6) oh yeah! the flash has stopped working, I googled it a bit and mostly on nokia forums and other forums I found out that this is a common issue, I mean common issue with such expensive hardware?
  

  7) One Note, you can make notes, but cant delete them? Maybe you can or I am just too dumb to find a way to delete them. I don't know, well.
  

  8) the nightmode in the camera is good, but you need a pair of very good hands, which dont shake even a bit, which means, if you are sitting somewhere, the photos in night will come out very good, but if you are standing and dont have very steady hands, forget the night mode.

column6: Why I would personally NOT RECOMMEND it wholeheartedly - though BRILLIANT PHONE
column7:
I'm a student of SciTech and I wanted a phone that would simplify my life by reducing the number of things I carry around in my pocket: to merge a phone with good reception, a great camera (can sneakily take great pictures inside classrooms even!), a mini-tablet that reads, writes, takes notes, translates etc, and easily synchs with my laptop. Also, incredibly durable.
  

  The natural choice was the best phone Nokia could make - from past experience - and luckily, it comes with a great camera.
  

  Am I satisfied? Well, here are the good points:
  

  1)Amazing touch sensitivity (I can navigate with my finger 1mm off the screen) and response - feels great to own
  

  2)good storage 32GB
  

  3)good battery - it only eats the battery when you are playing games, but performs reasonably well with movies and you can hear songs on it all day. Internet surfing time is pretty decent. Overnight, it was connected to wifi and updated all apps- I have a lot of apps - and synched facebook and gmail - after 24hrs it had lost 1% battery... brilliant!
  

  4) Very decent camera with good apps (look up Nokia Lenses). Android may have more variety though but then, the quality of images is brilliant only on the 920 overall, if you consider image resolution, quality, and stabilization. There is a button for camera and the camera can be accessed even when the screen is locked with a long press of the button - I don't know how many of you will appreciate the importance of this.
  

  5) I like the tiles - life is a lot more simpler, but miss the Live-wallpaper on Androids (not like I used it anyway, to conserve battery!) The interface is very simplified and nothing really is missing, unless you are a hellbent on having the Android screens. In fact, there is a nice feature called "hubs" which groups different kinds of apps together, which does look like the Android or iOs shells - but you can't modify it. Still, life is simpler - the pre-programmed grouping is convenient.
  

  6) I know the apps are terribly incompetent compared to Android but face it - the growth curve is sharper for WP8. I like the apps (but most of the good ones are not free, so beware). Most of the ones important to me are there. The Nokia specific apps are cool especially Cityscape. So dont get very worried that WP8 is primitive compared to Andrd and iOs (read: 10 Windows Phone 8 Features That Would Make Android Even Sweeter by Kavafian)
  

  7) Synchs pretty well with Windows7
  

  8) Looks beautiful, looks amazing (I have Matte black), is very strong and it's a little heavy but unlike what I feared - you don't feel the weight, even in your pocket. It's about 50-60g heavier than what most people are used to. Cmon, that's seriously not much!
  

  Some drawbacks.
  

  1) Non-removable battery, so you cannot carry a spare one around.
  
  2) Heats up randomly - while wirelessly charging, while playing for some while...
  
  These are synonymous with those of other highend, heavyduty smartphones also. We've been reduced to people who need to charge everyday and have started calling a good battery one which sees you through an entire day. Well, if you aren't gaming, LM920 is good in that respect, but an hour idling away playing games is a serious issue - eats up 20-30%!
  

  3) ONE TERRIBLE SHORTAGE...
  
  There is no ****** document manager. Sure it reads your PDF's and after a labourious process, reads your epubs also, but what sucks is that you cannot manage all these in folders! So if you are like me - this means scrolling through about 4000 files in one list (haven't uploaded them yet for this precise reason). I would really like a folder system - WP8 DEVELOPPERS DO SOMETHING!This is why I would not recommend a WP8, not just the Lumia 920.
  

  So am I in love with LM920? Yes! But given a chance to get the money back and invest in a different phone (like Samsung Note2?) would I do it? Yes. Definitely. This is because I REALLY MISS the folder system and the LM920 is making life hard here. Although, it's really fancy and will serve me well in parties and travel trips (as long as I carry a charger). So yeah, if you don't really care about these cons - LM920 IS the phone you want.

  -Multitasking- This is the one semi downside to this platform. It works for core apps, and WP has had it since Mango (WP7.5), but for some reason a lot of developers have not been able to make use of it. I can live with it, but I'm not really pleased with it as it is. I'm only hoping that at some stage, it gets pushed a little more to at least iOS levels.
  

  Camera- LOL, I was saving this for last, but then I realised that pretty much anything that had to be said has been said in countless reviews on the web. To sum it up, awesome low light stills and daylight/ low light video, not so outstanding, while still decent, stills in good light. The only thing I have to add, is that while the portico update was supposed to fix the blur, it hasn't completely achieved its goal. Check DP Reviews on that because for photography related reviews, that's where one goes, and not to tech sites which carry on their brand of fanboy journalism/ blogging.
  

  Outright negative aspects are
  
  -No core time suite (countdown timer/ stopwatch) app, Timers sometimes fail to buzz in the background or outright quit because the developers didn't code properly. The manufacturer should have provided this as a standard running in conjunction with the phone clock.
  

  -Volume settings get reverted to standard after a reboot and if you forget to push it up/ down, you have a ringer at an undesirable sound level. (I hope they see this as an obvious flaw and fix it.)
  

  Can't really think of much else, and to summarise my impression, I really like this device and am hopeful for the platform. It has a couple of problems, but at this stage in it's life, I think it is ahead of where the competition was.

column6: Switched from Samsung Galaxy S3 to lumia 720 to 920
column7:
I was a Nokia user a long time ago, N8 to 808 and 808 went to my wife and I got the Galaxy s3. Here are the reasons I switched from S3 to Windows Phone Nokia 720 to 920
  
  The 720 got wet in the rain and is beyond repair:(, and then I moved to 920 by selling my Galaxy S3.
  
  The point numbers match b/w the S3 and the 920
  
  1. The phone used to randomly reboot at times
  
  2. After about 100 hours of usage the phone would become very slow I had to reboot
  
  3. Unpredictable Battery life, I like to keep wifi on throughout the day. Suppose you forget to close some app, it drains your battery very quickly
  
  4. UI of the apps is too cluttered You have one big screen with lots of buttons here and there and each app can choose where it can place the buttons. with the huge screens of the S3/4 you have to reach your finger to the button from corner to corner, single handed use is impossible.
  
  5. Notorious apps than can suck your data plan and battery
  
  6. Call drops inside elevators at work (signal boosters installed in work place)
  
  7. lousy and pics/videos on the camera
  

  After switching to lumia
  
  1. Excellent Stablity, I don't know when my phone rebooted or when I rebooted, Reboots only when I run out of juice, which is again rare.
  
  2. excellent standby time. I unplug in the night and leave the phone on (wifi and mobile data shutoff) it is still 100 % in the morning. I use GPS tracking for 30 mins when I cycle to work, I reach office and it still is at 100 %!! that is insane. I never turn off GPS
  
  3. Windows phone, the OS has this thing called freeze, it shuts down apps that are not in background if there is no activity, that way even if I leave an app running It does not drain battery.
  
  4. Excellent UI and always predictable know where the menu's are located, and a simple swipe to right or left will get the job done. I always like the single handed use of the lumia 720, 920 is a bit large but I can still manage.
  
  5. Apps are not much, but more than enough for me, what ever apps are available they behave correctly and integrate well with the OS. MS has been doing some strict monitoring.
  
  6. I have not had a single call drop in elevators at work. If there is no signal, well nothing can be done about that, phone indicates that there is no signal.
  
  7. Excellent pics and Videos, I have the latest firmware, the older firmware had issues with colours and daylight photography. I get Excellent indoor shots as good as some compact cameras
  

  I am a power user, I have configured 4 email ID's on the phone, my work email is set sync as the mail arrives all other email sync every hour, facebook, google contacts, I have about 10 games, I play about 15 to 30 mins daily. I mainly use for facebook and email. sometimes Youtube. MS took the you-tube app off :(
  
  I am impressed with the phone,
  
  The only thing nagging me is the Volume control, the Volume control from speaker and headphone is the same :( It is the stupidest thing in the phone. I hope it gets fixed in the upcoming update from MS.
  
  BTW I did not buy the phone from flipkart.

Having used a variety of smartphones, I was a bit sceptical when I heard Nokia had launched its own series of Lumia smartphones. The brand has been an icon of reliability, but for some apparent reason, had fallen behind its competitors when it came to smartphones. But, when I could not resist the allure and got my hands on the Nokia Lumia 920, I was in for a real surprise. This smartphone is surely one of the most innovative devices to be ever launched by Nokia.
  

  The unibody polycarbonate design of my Lumia 920 is not like anything I have seen yet, and it comes in such vibrantly coloured covers. The camera on my new Nokia smartphone is a whopping 8.7 MP rear shooter that comes with a cutting-edge and sophisticated Carl Zeiss Tessar lens. Integrating PureView camera technology and optical image stabilisation, this camera renders all my photographs in pristine quality, almost as if shot by a professional photographer. Also included, is a dual LED flash that lights up the night and allows low-light imaging.
  

  The screen of my Lumia 920 is a 4.5-inch LCD touch display that features PureMotion HD+ technology. It responds quickly to my touch and can also be used when wearing gloves. The curved design of the display provides enhanced readability in direct sunlight. With Corning Gorilla Glass 2 protection, this tough display easily weathers my rough use. The Windows Phone 8 operating system in my Lumia 920 is a breakthrough in terms of convenience and navigation. It comes with features like PeopleHub that helps me tag all my frequently used contacts to my home screen. All their social networking updates reach me directly, without the effort of logging into these sites and browsing to their profiles. The Live Tiles interface lets me arrange all my frequently used apps and games on my home screen. Microsoft Office comes pre-installed on my phone and the support for MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint make work on the move, really simple and enjoyable. I also use the integrated MS Outlook app for managing my emails.
  

  My Lumia 920 outperforms quite a few of its contemporaries due to its dual core 1.5 GHz GHz Qualcomm Snapdragon S4 'Krait' mobile processor, an Adreno 225 graphics chip and 1 GB RAM. This makes multitasking a breeze and lets me play HD games and execute memory-intensive apps. Storing data is also not a problem, as I can use the 32 GB onboard memory. Additionally, Nokia also provides complimentary SkyDrive storage for additional data needs.
  

  When on the move, I do not like to ask for directions to my destination. This is where the Nokia Maps and Nokia Drive apps of my Lumia 920 come in handy. They provide me with turn by turn directions even when I am not subscribed to data usage. On the connectivity front, my Lumia 920 comes with Wi-Fi, WLAN, NFC and Bluetooth which makes exchanging files and accessing the web all the more easy.

The latest phone I have bought for myself is the Nokia Lumia 920 as I needed a break from the monotonous Android and wanted to try Windows Phone OS. The phone has come as a breeze of rejuvenating air and instilled great interest and excitement in me. First of all, my phone has a sturdy and sleek polycarbonate design that fits comfortably in my hand. It comes in attractive snap-on covers of cyan, red, yellow, black and white colours that effortlessly display my style and attitude. I have taken a liking for the tiled interface that the OS brings to the table.
  
  One of the first things I've noticed in the phone is its display and to sum it up in one word: gorgeous. The phone also flaunts Nokia's ClearBlack technology that provides me enhanced contrast and legibility even in direct sunlight. The screen also sports PureMotion HD+ which is a combination of HD display, super-sensitive screen and a super-fast 60 Hz display. column6: I DON'T AGREE WITH MR. JAM'S REVIEW!!
column7:
A smartphone without apps is incomplete. I don't expect anybody to buy a phone costing around 40k and wait for apps to appear. Even if you wait, it's a waste of time as Mr Jam's review is dated 18 Jan and it's May and still there are a handful of games available on the Windows store. Basic games like Temple run also lag on the lumia 920, what more can you expect from the other windows devices. Don't believe me, just check out the reviews on the windows store.I have seen mid range phone like the galaxy s advance (rooted) handling games like MC 4 smoothly and it costs only 15k.
  

  Another disappointment is that almost all the games are paid versions unlike android and ios which have plethora of free games. You need not spend more money on apps after buying an expensive phone. It really matters for a student's. I cant shed all my pocket money buying apps.
  
  Regarding the memory 32 GB must be enough for most of the people out there but expandability is always a better option for folks with a lot of stuff. And please don't say that memory cards slow down a phone. I don't know why Mr Jam said this (probably he tried a class 4 card with Galaxy S3). UHS cards are available and they offer speeds greater than  50-60 mbps. What more do you need.
  
  Regarding the display, well it is one's own opinion. I still love the saturation of the hd super amoled display on the S3 and note 2. Some may find the lcd display on lumia 920 more appealing. Whatever it is, super amoled panels use much less power than LCD an also occupy less space(leading to a thinner phone). And you call a 2000mah battery a "bigger battery". Come on... the battery is non removable. A larger battery would have been a better deal(considering the size of the phone).
  
  The lumia 920 is a good device but Windows phone 8 spoils the party. A device like this with android 4.2 would have been a way better deal.
  
  Giving 2 stars because i just love the internet explorer 10.

I bought a Lumia 920 in March 2013 from The Mobile Store Gurgaon at INR 37000, and just within 4 days of buying it, the phone crashed. The phone would just hang up whenever I started the camera and only a hard reset could bring the phone back. I went to the local Nokia Care and they said it will be repaired. I requested a replacement and I was turned down. Then I wrote to Stephen Elop, then CEO of Nokia about this and within 4 days I got a brand new piece. I was grateful about the prompt customer care experience.
  

  I still faced hang-ups whenever I would use Here Maps and Here applications. But in the meantime, my sim got disconnected and I could not test this further. For about an year, I used this mobile only for photos, music and data storing/editing. Here too I wrote a mail to Stephen Elop, but I guess by then my emails may have been tagged as spam in Stephen's inbox.
  

  After I was transferred to Pune, in July 2014, I bought a new sim and the hang-up issues resurfaced. One fine day, after 2 hours of charging, the screen stopped working. I again went to the local Nokia Care and they said that the screen needs to be replaced and I will be charged INR 13500 for the same because my phone's warranty expired in May 2014.
  

  This time too I wrote to Stephen Elop, and this time too no response from him. Instead I got a response from India Repair Manager that they will provide me concession and I will have to pay INR 8200 + Taxes. I requested to know the reason for this failure even after handling the mobile as delicately as possible, but nobody cared to respond on that. Instead I got a follow-up email asking my opinion about the concession provided.
  

  I was a fan of Nokia and that is the reason I have bought 3 Nokia phones till date viz. 3315, X6 and Lumia 920. I have also used Motorola, Blackberry, Micromax, Ericsson, and all of these phones are still working including X6 and 3315. But Lumia 920 has turned out to be the worst mobile I have ever used even after it being a smartphone. And on top of that, the customer care experience has been so GOOD (sarcastically), that I would recommend a Noble Prize for Nokia Customer Care.

column6: Decent hardware with not so good OS
column7:
Hi all,
  
  First of all I gave this product 2 stars based purely on my personal experience with this phone for 6 months (i would like to mention that I am a heavy user of smartphones), so Lumia lovers - no hard feelings.
  

  Prior to owning this phone, i used S3 and I was totally in love with it, I am not going to write about my experience with it here though. I lost it in an accident and was in search of a worthy successor and after lot of research and to satisfy my itch to try new platform, I bought this phone and from day one I absolutely hate it. Here are my reasons:
  

  Interface:
  
  MS has made WP8 very intutively and also been successful in creating an almost crash free OS, no doubt about that. But, doing this, they have made the OS so light that interface looks boring (tiles-many of you might like this but I dont).
  
  Also, doing anything in this phone is not as easy as in an android phone like switching on/off the bluetooth, GPS, WIFI, mobile data, flight mode etc etc.. For everthing I need to go to settings and navigate from there
  
  If I am in an application like Gmaps or watching videos and then I receive a message, I need to exit to main screen open the mesage app and then see the message. Just a swiping for notification will do the job in android.
  

  Battery icon, network strength, bluetooth/wifi status etc are shown at the top of the screen, which is good, but why the hell they are hidden all the time? This phone wont notify me untill the battery gets critically low and the I have to run for charging point. Also if i forget to swith wifi/mobile data/bluetooth off, i should be able to see something on the screen which will notify me that they are still on, if they are hidden, i would not know their status.
  

  Sharing
  
  Everytime I want to share a pic, i need to go to home screen , then go to settings, open the bluetooth and switch it on and go back all the way and then share the pic. If bluetooth is off, then "bluetooth" wont show up in the sharing list and it would not ask me if i want to switch it on or not. Android will ask let me know if bluetooth is off and ask me if i would like to switch it on or not.
  

  lockscreen:
  
  Android shows every notification related every app installed in the phone in lock screen when it is locked. But I have to bloody choose from the list of apps in my phone in lumia and thats all, it wont show the notifications for which i have not selected.
  

  Internet explorer
  
  I dont think I should write much about this as all of you know about it.
  

  Media
  
  Nokia Music is one of the two reasons why I choose to give 2 stars for this phone. Musicis absolutely mind blowing and the dolby make it one of the best in the market. And 1 year free subscription is a boon and the app is absolutely stunning.
  

  Video watching is great but there are some irritating points here like the screen ans capacitive buttons are always active. If i touch anyone of them, it responds and navigates away from the video. If I try to lock the phone, the whole phone is locked stopping the video. Android phones lock the phone and the screen but leave the video on. Even if i accedentally touch the screen or the capacitive buttons, it shows that the phone is locked, how cool is that?
  

  Hardware
  
  This is where it earns another star from me, its just astounding. its rock solid and screen is great, camera is next to god and designe is amazing. I totally love the hardware, I wish android were there in the phone instead of WP8
  

  Finally, I think I made a biggest mistake of my like buying this phone, i feel like this because may be because I came from android platform. I strongly think that people who love this phone are from IOS platform or new to smartphone world or haven't used android properly. My suggestion - DO NOT BUY!!!!
